title.zh: 卷406 列傳一百九十三 骆秉章 胡林翼
title.en: Volume 406 Biographies 193: Luo Bingzhang, Hu Linyi
title.raw: 卷406 列傳一百九十三 骆秉章 胡林翼

sentences.zh: 列傳一百九十三

translations.literal: Biography 193.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 193.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章胡林翼

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang; Hu Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang and Hu Linyi.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章，原名俊，以字行，改字籥門，廣東花縣人。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang, original name Jun, styled himself by his courtesy name, later changed his courtesy name to Yuemen, was a native of Huaxian in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Bingzhang, whose original name was Jun and who was commonly known by his courtesy name, later changed that name to Yuemen; he came from Huaxian in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed editor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1832, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made an editor.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，稽察銀庫，卻陋規，嚴檢閱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor, inspected the silver treasury, refused improper customary fees, and strictly supervised examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he audited the silver treasury, rejected customary kickbacks, and enforced inspections rigorously.

sentences.zh: 吏不便其所為，欲齮齕去之，會發其奸，不得逞。

translations.literal: Clerks were inconvenienced by his conduct and wished to slander and remove him; coincidentally their malfeasance was exposed, and they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks resented his ways and tried to slander him out of office, but their own corruption came to light, and the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 歷給事中、鴻臚寺少卿、奉天府丞兼學政。

translations.literal: He successively served as supervising secretary, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and deputy magistrate of Fengtian prefecture concurrently as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of supervising secretary, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Fengtian deputy magistrate with concurrent duties as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，銀庫虧帑事發，坐失察，褫職，罰分賠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the silver treasury deficit was exposed; he was punished for lax supervision, stripped of office, and fined to share in restitution.
translations.idiomatic: In 1843 the treasury shortfall came to light; blamed for failing to detect it, he was dismissed and ordered to pay part of the loss.

sentences.zh: 及讞定，宣宗知秉章獨持正無私，特旨以庶子用。

translations.literal: When the case was finalized, Emperor Xuanzong knew Bingzhang alone had been upright and selfless, and specially ordered him employed as a subordinate mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the judgment was settled, the Daoguang Emperor, knowing that Bingzhang alone had acted with rectitude and no private interest, specially ordered him restored as a subordinate tutor in the heir apparent's academy.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，補右庶子，先後命赴山東、河南、江蘇按事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed right subordinate mentor and was successively ordered to investigate affairs in Shandong, Henan, and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made right subordinate tutor and was repeatedly sent to investigate cases in Shandong, Henan, and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 詞臣奉使出異數，所治獄悉稱旨。

translations.literal: For a literary official to be sent on imperial commission was an unusual honor; every case he handled fully met the throne's intent.
translations.idiomatic: It was rare for a literary official to be dispatched on such missions, and every case he handled won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 出為湖北按察使，遷貴州布政使，調雲南。

translations.literal: He went out as judicial commissioner of Hubei, was transferred to provincial treasurer of Guizhou, and then reassigned to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as Hubei judicial commissioner, then became Guizhou provincial treasurer before being transferred to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted to governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1850 he was appointed governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，廣西匪熾，詔湖廣總督程矞採赴湖南督辦防務，秉章及提督-{余}-萬清副之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the rebels in Guangxi grew fierce; the Huguang governor-general Cheng Yucai was ordered to Hunan to supervise defenses, with Bingzhang and regional commander Yu Wanqing assisting him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851, as rebellion in Guangxi intensified, Governor-General Cheng Yucai of Huguang was ordered to Hunan to oversee defenses, assisted by Bingzhang and Regional Commander Yu Wanqing.

sentences.zh: 大學士賽尚阿督師過境，以供張薄，有嫌，密奏湖南吏治廢弛。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sai Shanga passed through commanding the army; because provisions and entertainment were meager he bore a grudge and secretly memorialized that Hunan's official administration was lax.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sai Shanga passed through at the head of the army; resenting the scant hospitality, he secretly reported that Hunan's administration had fallen into disorder.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔秉章開缺來京，而粵匪已由桂林北竄入湖南。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict removed Bingzhang from office and summoned him to the capital, while the Guangdong rebels had already fled north from Guilin into Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852 he was ordered to vacate his post and come to Beijing, even as the rebels had already broken north from Guilin into Hunan.

sentences.zh: 矞採聞警，由衡州退長沙，尋復往駐。

translations.literal: Yucai heard the alarm, retreated from Hengzhou to Changsha, and soon returned to take up station again.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Yucai withdrew from Hengzhou to Changsha and soon returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 萬清守道州，被賊陷。

translations.literal: Wanqing defended Daozhou and was overrun by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing held Daozhou but the city fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 江華、嘉禾、桂陽、郴州、攸縣相繼失，萬清逮治。

translations.literal: Jianghua, Jiahe, Guiyang, Chenzhou, and Youxian fell in succession, and Wanqing was arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jianghua, Jiahe, Guiyang, Chenzhou, and Youxian fell one after another, and Wanqing was arrested.

sentences.zh: 秉章坐未能預防，革職留任。

translations.literal: Bingzhang was punished for failing to take preventive measures, stripped of office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang was stripped of rank for failing to prevent the losses but was kept in office.

sentences.zh: 先議修長沙城，甫畢工，而賊由醴陵突犯長沙。

translations.literal: Repairs to the walls of Changsha had just been completed when the rebels burst from Liling to strike the city.
translations.idiomatic: Work on Changsha's walls had only just finished when the rebels surged in from Liling to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 秉章嬰城固守，悍賊蕭朝貴預诇城壞，故以輕軍來襲，未得逞，尋斃於砲。

translations.literal: Bingzhang closed the gates and held firm; the fierce rebel Xiao Chaogui had reconnoitered and found the walls weak, so he came with a light force to raid but did not succeed, and was soon killed by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang sealed the city and held on. The fierce rebel Xiao Chaogui, having scouted weak points in the walls, led a light force to raid but failed; he was soon killed by artillery.

sentences.zh: 副將鄧紹良赴援最先至，入城任戰守。

translations.literal: Brigade general Deng Shaoliang was the first to arrive in relief and entered the city to take charge of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade General Deng Shaoliang was first to reach the city with reinforcements and took charge of its defense.

sentences.zh: 賊屢以地雷壞城，皆擊卻之。

translations.literal: The rebels repeatedly used land mines to breach the walls, but each attempt was beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels repeatedly tried to blast the walls with mines, but each assault was repulsed.

sentences.zh: 新授巡撫張亮基至，秉章奉旨暫留同守城。

translations.literal: The newly appointed governor Zhang Liangji arrived, and Bingzhang was ordered by edict to remain temporarily and defend the city together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the newly appointed governor Zhang Liangji arrived, Bingzhang was ordered to stay and help defend the city.

sentences.zh: 及賊首洪秀全大舉來攻，援軍向榮、和春、張國梁等亦並集，且守且戰，歷八十餘日。

translations.literal: When the rebel leader Hong Xiuquan came in force to attack, relief armies under Xiang Rong, He Chun, Zhang Guoliang, and others also gathered; they defended and fought for more than eighty days.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan brought his main force to besiege the city, reinforcements under Xiang Rong, He Chun, Zhang Guoliang, and others also arrived; the defenders held and fought for more than eighty days.

sentences.zh: 賊引去，陷岳州，趨湖北。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew, took Yuezhou, and pressed toward Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew, captured Yuezhou, and marched toward Hubei.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿、程矞採並坐失機罷譴。

translations.literal: Sai Shanga and Cheng Yucai were both punished for missing their opportunity and dismissed in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Sai Shanga and Cheng Yucai were both disgraced and dismissed for having lost the initiative.

sentences.zh: 秉章以守城功，免議，召來京。

translations.literal: Bingzhang, for his merit in defending the city, was exempted from censure and summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in defending the city, Bingzhang was spared further punishment and summoned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 尋命留湖北襄辦防守事宜，未至而武昌陷。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to remain in Hubei to assist in defense, but before he arrived Wuchang fell.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to stay in Hubei to help with defense, but Wuchang fell before he could take up the assignment.

sentences.zh: 三年春，官軍收復武昌，暫署湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year government troops recovered Wuchang, and he served temporarily as governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1853 government forces retook Wuchang, and he served briefly as acting governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 詔赴徐州筦糧台，未行，复署湖南巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to the grain depot at Xuzhou; before he departed he was again made acting governor of Hunan, and soon received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to the grain depot at Xuzhou, but before he left he was again made acting governor of Hunan and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 在籍侍郎曾國籓奉命治團練，始立湘軍，秉章力贊成之。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, a metropolitan graduate on leave serving as vice minister, was ordered to organize militia training and first established the Hunan Army; Bingzhang strongly supported the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, a metropolitan graduate serving at home as vice minister, was ordered to organize militia and founded what became the Hunan Army; Bingzhang gave the project his full support.

sentences.zh: 又延湘陰舉人左宗棠襄理戎幕，廣羅英俊之士，練勇助剿，軍威漸振。

translations.literal: He also retained the Xiangyin licentiate Zuo Zongtang to assist in the military staff, widely recruited talented men, trained braves to aid in suppression, and military prestige gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He also brought in the Xiangyin scholar Zuo Zongtang to run his military staff, recruited able men widely, trained local militia to join the campaigns, and the army's standing gradually recovered.

sentences.zh: 先清境內，遣軍分路破江西賊於桂陽，破廣西賊於永明、零陵、江華，破廣東賊於興寧，又破江西賊於茶陵，而常寧、永興土匪皆平。

translations.literal: First he cleared the interior, sent armies by separate routes to defeat Jiangxi rebels at Guiyang, Guangxi rebels at Yongming, Lingling, and Jianghua, Guangdong rebels at Xingning, and again Jiangxi rebels at Chaling, while bandits in Changning and Yongxing were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He first secured the province, sending columns to defeat Jiangxi rebels at Guiyang, Guangxi rebels at Yongming, Lingling, and Jianghua, Guangdong rebels at Xingning, and Jiangxi rebels again at Chaling, while bandits in Changning and Yongxing were also suppressed.

sentences.zh: 賊由湖北進陷岳州，令王珍、曾國葆水陸截擊，敗之，岳州遂復。

translations.literal: Rebels advancing from Hubei took Yuezhou; he ordered Wang Zhen and Zeng Guobao to intercept them by land and water, defeated them, and Yuezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels advancing from Hubei captured Yuezhou, he sent Wang Zhen and Zeng Guobao to cut them off by land and water, defeated them, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 令貴州道員胡林翼率黔勇追賊逼界口。

translations.literal: He ordered the Guizhou circuit intendant Hu Linyi to lead Guizhou braves in pursuit, pressing the rebels to the border pass.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guizhou circuit intendant Hu Linyi to lead Guizhou troops in pursuit, driving the rebels to the border.

sentences.zh: 四年，總督吳文鎔師潰黃州，漢陽复陷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Governor-General Wu Wenrong's army was routed at Huangzhou and Hanyang again fell.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 Governor-General Wu Wenrong's army was routed at Huangzhou and Hanyang fell again.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓水師成，進援湖北，前敵失利，岳州复陷。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan's river force was completed and advanced to aid Hubei; the vanguard suffered defeat and Yuezhou again fell.
translations.idiomatic: After Zeng Guofan's river flotilla was ready, it advanced to aid Hubei, but the vanguard was beaten and Yuezhou fell again.

sentences.zh: 賊犯靖港及樟樹港，距長沙數十里，並陷寧鄉、湘潭。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked Jinggang and Zhangshugang, within several tens of li of Changsha, and also took Ningxiang and Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels struck Jinggang and Zhangshugang, only a few dozen li from Changsha, and also captured Ningxiang and Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 秉章調撫標兵益塔齊布軍，令偕楊岳斌、彭玉麟同援湘潭。

translations.literal: Bingzhang transferred Hunan provincial troops to reinforce Taqibu’s army and ordered them together with Yang Yuebin and Peng Yulin to relieve Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang detached Hunan provincial troops to reinforce Taqibu's force and ordered them, together with Yang Yuebin and Peng Yulin, to relieve Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 國籓親率水師戰靖港，复失利。

translations.literal: Guofan personally led the river force to fight at Jinggang and again suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan personally led the river flotilla into battle at Jinggang and was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 布政使徐有壬、按察使陶恩培請奏劾罷其軍。

translations.literal: Provincial treasurer Xu Youren and judicial commissioner Tao Enpei requested a memorial impeaching him and disbanding his army.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial treasurer Xu Youren and judicial commissioner Tao Enpei asked the throne to impeach Zeng and disband his forces.

sentences.zh: 秉章曰：「曾公謀國之忠，不可以一時勝敗論也。

translations.literal: Bingzhang said: "Lord Zeng's loyalty in planning for the state cannot be judged by momentary victory or defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang said, "Lord Zeng's loyalty to the state cannot be judged by a single battle's outcome."

sentences.zh: 」會次日塔齊布等大破賊於湘潭，復其城，靖港賊亦遁走，長沙獲安。

translations.literal: The next day Taqibu and others inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Xiangtan and recovered the city; the rebels at Jinggang also fled, and Changsha was secured.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Taqibu and his colleagues routed the rebels at Xiangtan and retook the city; the force at Jinggang also withdrew, and Changsha was safe.

sentences.zh: 賊繞西湖陷華容、龍陽、常德，令胡林翼專剿此路。

translations.literal: Rebels skirted West Lake and took Huarong, Longyang, and Changde; he ordered Hu Linyi to concentrate on suppressing this route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swung around West Lake and captured Huarong, Longyang, and Changde; he put Hu Linyi in charge of clearing that line.

sentences.zh: 塔齊布、羅澤南進規岳州、崇陽、通城，未幾，各城皆复，而武昌再陷。

translations.literal: Taqibu and Luo Zeyuan advanced to recover Yuezhou, Chongyang, and Tongcheng; before long each city was retaken, but Wuchang again fell.
translations.idiomatic: Taqibu and Luo Zeyuan pressed to retake Yuezhou, Chongyang, and Tongcheng; soon each city was recovered, but Wuchang fell again.

sentences.zh: 國籓整軍東征，餉械悉力資之無缺，十月，遂克武昌。

translations.literal: Guofan reorganized the army for the eastern campaign; Bingzhang supplied pay and arms to the full without shortage, and in the tenth month Wuchang was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan reorganized his army for the eastern campaign, and Bingzhang supplied funds and weapons without stint; in October Wuchang was captured.

sentences.zh: 湘軍之名自此顯。

translations.literal: The name of the Hunan Army became prominent from this time.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the Hunan Army made its name.

sentences.zh: 五年，武昌三陷，胡林翼署巡撫，飛書告急。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wuchang fell for the third time; Hu Linyi served as acting governor and sent urgent dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 Wuchang fell for the third time; Hu Linyi, now acting governor, sent urgent appeals for help.

sentences.zh: 秉章令鮑超率水師先赴，彭玉麟募勇繼之。

translations.literal: Bingzhang ordered Bao Chao to lead the river force there first and Peng Yulin to recruit braves to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang sent Bao Chao ahead with the river flotilla and had Peng Yulin raise more troops to follow.

sentences.zh: 起楊岳斌於家，統其眾以固北路，而南路廣東、廣西群賊擾境，土匪紛起應之。

translations.literal: Yang Yuebin was recalled from retirement to command his followers and secure the northern route, while on the southern route Guangdong and Guangxi rebel bands harassed the border and local bandits rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuebin was called back from retirement to hold the northern line, even as rebel bands from Guangdong and Guangxi raided the southern border and local bandits rose to join them.

sentences.zh: 令田興恕禦東路，王珍剿南路，先清土匪，克東安，斬廣西賊首胡有祿。

translations.literal: He ordered Tian Xingyu to guard the eastern route and Wang Zhen to suppress the southern route, first clearing local bandits, taking Dong'an, and beheading the Guangxi rebel leader Hu Youlu.
translations.idiomatic: He put Tian Xingyu on the eastern front and Wang Zhen on the south, cleared the local bandits first, captured Dong'an, and killed the Guangxi rebel leader Hu Youlu.

sentences.zh: 餘賊复擾永明、江華，擊走之。

translations.literal: Remaining rebels again harassed Yongming and Jianghua and were driven off.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels raided Yongming and Jianghua again and were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 克桂陽、永興、茶陵、郴州、宜章，斃廣東賊首何祿，南路遂定。

translations.literal: Guiyang, Yongxing, Chaling, Chenzhou, and Yizhang were taken, the Guangdong rebel leader He Lu was killed, and the southern route was settled.
translations.idiomatic: His forces retook Guiyang, Yongxing, Chaling, Chenzhou, and Yizhang, killed the Guangdong rebel leader He Lu, and secured the south.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗犯晃州、沅州、麻陽，並擊走之。

translations.literal: Miao from Guizhou raided Huangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Mayang, and were all beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Miao raiders from Guizhou struck Huangzhou, Yuanzhou, and Mayang, and were driven off in each case.

sentences.zh: 當武昌陷後，總督楊霈奏飭胡林翼渡江上扼漢川，以固荊襄。

translations.literal: After Wuchang fell, Governor-General Yang Fu memorialized ordering Hu Linyi to cross the river and hold Hanchuan upstream to secure Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchang fell, Governor-General Yang Fu memorialized ordering Hu Linyi to cross the Yangzi and hold Hanchuan to secure the Jing-Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 秉章上疏爭之，略曰：「楊霈始終堅執防賊北竄，然以現在形勢論之，江西、湖南尚稱完地。

translations.literal: Bingzhang memorialized in opposition, stating in summary: "Yang Fu has consistently insisted on guarding against the rebels fleeing north, yet judging the present situation, Jiangxi and Hunan may still be called intact territory."
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang submitted a counter-memorial, arguing in essence: "Yang Fu has always insisted on blocking a northern rebel breakout, yet as matters stand Jiangxi and Hunan are still largely intact."

sentences.zh: 若使湖北水陸兩軍移駐漢川，長江千里，盡委之賊，其將置東南於不問乎？

translations.literal: If Hubei's land and river forces are shifted to garrison Hanchuan, the thousand li of the Yangzi would be wholly abandoned to the rebels—would the southeast then be left unattended?
translations.idiomatic: If Hubei's land and river armies are moved to Hanchuan, a thousand li of the Yangzi would be handed to the rebels—are we to abandon the southeast entirely?

sentences.zh: 未解者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is my first objection.

sentences.zh: 移駐漢川，祗能禦上竄襄陽之路，其於荊州並無輕重。

translations.literal: Stationing at Hanchuan can only block the route of rebels fleeing upstream toward Xiangyang; it has no bearing on the importance of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A post at Hanchuan could only block rebels moving up toward Xiangyang; it would do nothing for Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 若賊水陸並進，荊州門戶，其孰當之？

translations.literal: If the rebels advance by land and water together, who will stand at the gateway of Jingzhou?
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels advance by land and water together, who will hold the gateway of Jingzhou?

sentences.zh: 未解者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second point I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is my second objection.

sentences.zh: 水陸兩軍相為依附，胡林翼既駐漢川，則水軍非退守監利，即移泊岳州，為湖南門戶計，尚未為失。

translations.literal: The land and river forces depend on each other; once Hu Linyi is stationed at Hanchuan, the river force must either fall back to Jianli or anchor at Yuezhou—for Hunan's gateway this would not yet count as a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Land and river forces must support each other; once Hu Linyi is at Hanchuan, the flotilla would have to fall back to Jianli or anchor at Yuezhou—which might still serve Hunan's interests.

sentences.zh: 然武漢門戶豈能度外置之乎？

translations.literal: Yet can the gateway of Wuhan be set aside as if it did not matter?
translations.idiomatic: But can we simply write off the gateway of Wuhan?

sentences.zh: 未解者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is my third objection.

sentences.zh: 若謂賊眾兵單，不思廣濟失利之初，以總督萬餘之兵，不能當千餘之賊，乃退守黃州，未一日即退漢川，由此而德安，而隨州，今又退至棗陽。

translations.literal: If one says the rebels are many and our troops few, one does not recall how at the first defeat at Guangji the governor-general's force of more than ten thousand could not withstand a little over a thousand rebels, and retreated to defend Huangzhou; within a day he fell back to Hanchuan, then to De'an, then Suizhou, and now again to Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: If the claim is that the rebels outnumber us, consider the first defeat at Guangji: the governor-general's army of more than ten thousand could not hold off a little over a thousand rebels, retreated to Huangzhou, fell back to Hanchuan within a day, then to De'an, Suizhou, and now Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 北竄者賊也，引之北竄者誰歟？

translations.literal: Those who flee north are the rebels—but who is it that leads them north?
translations.idiomatic: It is the rebels who flee north—but who is driving them north?

sentences.zh: 未解者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth point I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fourth objection.

sentences.zh: 扼賊北竄，必固荊襄，欲保荊襄，必守武漢，此一定之局。

translations.literal: To block the rebels' northern flight one must secure Jing and Xiang; to preserve Jing and Xiang one must hold Wuhan—this is a fixed strategic pattern.
translations.idiomatic: To stop a northern breakout one must hold Jing and Xiang; to hold Jing and Xiang one must hold Wuhan—that is the fixed pattern of the war.

sentences.zh: 漢陽未復，不能繞至漢川，況武漢均為賊屯，胡林翼縱至漢川，以孤軍駐四面皆賊之地，又能為荊襄門戶計乎？

translations.literal: With Hanyang not yet recovered one cannot even detour to Hanchuan; moreover Wuhan is all in rebel hands—if Hu Linyi goes to Hanchuan anyway and stations a lone force surrounded by enemies on every side, how can he still plan for the gateway of Jing and Xiang?
translations.idiomatic: With Hanyang still in rebel hands one cannot even reach Hanchuan; Wuhan is entirely enemy-held. If Hu Linyi goes to Hanchuan with a lone detachment surrounded on every side, how can he guard the gateway of Jing and Xiang?

sentences.zh: 未解者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth point I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is my fifth objection.

sentences.zh: 」霈之專防北竄，原出迎合上意。

translations.literal: Fu's exclusive focus on blocking northern flight originally arose from catering to the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's obsession with blocking a northern breakout arose from pandering to the throne.

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔斥所詆霈者過當。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, an edict rebuked the slander of Fu as excessive.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, an edict rebuked Bingzhang for going too far in attacking Fu.

sentences.zh: 然上意開悟，未久罷霈，以官文代之，與胡林翼合規武漢。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's mind was enlightened; before long Fu was dismissed and Guan Wen replaced him, joining with Hu Linyi to plan the recovery of Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne took his point; Fu was soon dismissed, Guan Wen replaced him, and together with Hu Linyi they turned to recovering Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 秉章悉力資給林翼軍，如所以助曾國籓者。

translations.literal: Bingzhang supplied Linyi's army to the full, just as he had aided Zeng Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang supplied Hu Linyi's army without stint, just as he had supported Zeng Guofan.

sentences.zh: 洎林翼與羅澤南破石達開於咸寧，達開折入江西，連陷瑞州、臨江，而吉安、撫州、建昌屬城多被擾。

translations.literal: When Linyi and Luo Zeyuan defeated Shi Dakai at Xianning, Dakai turned into Jiangxi and in succession took Ruizhou and Linjiang, while many subordinate cities of Ji'an, Fuzhou, and Jianchang were harassed.
translations.idiomatic: After Linyi and Luo Zeyuan defeated Shi Dakai at Xianning, Dakai swung into Jiangxi, captured Ruizhou and Linjiang in succession, and raided many counties under Ji'an, Fuzhou, and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 國籓自上年九江之挫，久留南昌，孤軍難進展。

translations.literal: Guofan, since last year's defeat at Jiujiang, had long remained at Nanchang, and his isolated army found it hard to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Since his defeat at Jiujiang the year before, Guofan had lingered at Nanchang with an isolated force that could make little headway.

sentences.zh: 秉章至是銳意東援，令江忠濟出通城以固岳州，令劉長佑、蕭啟江率軍分路入江西。

translations.literal: Bingzhang now pressed an eastern relief effort, ordered Jiang Zhongji to move out from Tongcheng to secure Yuezhou, and ordered Liu Changyou and Xiao Qijiang to lead armies by separate routes into Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang now threw himself into eastern relief, sending Jiang Zhongji out from Tongcheng to secure Yuezhou and Liu Changyou and Xiao Qijiang into Jiangxi by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 六年，劉長佑等連克萍鄉、萬載，進攻袁州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Liu Changyou and others in succession took Pingxiang and Wanzai and advanced to attack Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856 Liu Changyou and his colleagues captured Pingxiang and Wanzai in succession and advanced on Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 江忠濟戰歿通城，以王珍代之，連克通城、崇陽、蒲圻、通山諸縣。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongji died in battle at Tongcheng; Wang Zhen replaced him and in succession recovered Tongcheng, Chongyang, Puqi, and Tongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongji was killed at Tongcheng; Wang Zhen replaced him and retook Tongcheng, Chongyang, Puqi, and Tongshan in succession.

sentences.zh: 至冬，長佑克袁州、分宜、新喻，趙煥聯自茶陵收永寧，-{余}-星元自酃縣收永新、蓮花廳。

translations.literal: By winter Changyou took Yuanzhou, Fenyi, and Xinyu; Zhao Huanlian from Chaling recovered Yongning, and Yu Xingyuan from Lingxian recovered Yongxin and Lianhua subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By winter Changyou had taken Yuanzhou, Fenyi, and Xinyu; Zhao Huanlian advanced from Chaling to recover Yongning, and Yu Xingyuan from Lingxian to recover Yongxin and Lianhua.

sentences.zh: 初議規江西分三路，北路出瑞州，中路出袁州，南路出吉安。

translations.literal: At first the plan to recover Jiangxi divided into three routes: the northern route out of Ruizhou, the central route out of Yuanzhou, and the southern route out of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: The original plan for Jiangxi divided forces into three routes: north from Ruizhou, center from Yuanzhou, and south from Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑袁州一路兵逾九千，餉難再籌。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou's Yuanzhou route already had more than nine thousand troops, and further pay was hard to raise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou's Yuanzhou column already exceeded nine thousand men, and further funds were hard to find.

sentences.zh: 至是始令周鳳山、曾國荃各募勇二千，合趨吉安。

translations.literal: Only now were Zhou Fengshan and Zeng Guoquan each ordered to recruit two thousand braves and together press toward Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were Zhou Fengshan and Zeng Guoquan each told to raise two thousand men and advance together on Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉秉章不分畛域，越境殄寇，賜花翎。

translations.literal: An edict praised Bingzhang for not distinguishing territorial boundaries and crossing borders to exterminate bandits, and bestowed the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Bingzhang for crossing provincial lines to destroy the rebels and awarded him the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 七年，武漢既復，下游無警，湘軍乃四出。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, once Wuhan was recovered and the lower reaches were free of alarm, the Hunan Army marched out in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857, with Wuhan recovered and the lower Yangzi secure, the Hunan Army fanned out on every front.

sentences.zh: 以蔣益澧率永州軍援廣西，以王珍軍增援江西，以兆琛等軍援貴州，需餉益鉅。

translations.literal: Jiang Yili led the Yongzhou army to aid Guangxi, Wang Zhen's force reinforced Jiangxi, and Zhao Chen and others aided Guizhou; the need for pay grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yili led Yongzhou troops to aid Guangxi, Wang Zhen reinforced Jiangxi, and Zhao Chen and others aided Guizhou, and the demand for funds grew sharply.

sentences.zh: 湖南自軍興停漕運，米賤，而徵折猶沿舊價，民困賦絀。

translations.literal: Since the war began Hunan had halted grain transport tribute; rice was cheap, yet tax conversion still followed old prices, the people were distressed and revenue fell short.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began Hunan had stopped the grain tribute transport; rice was cheap, yet tax assessments still used old rates, leaving the people strained and revenue short.

sentences.zh: 秉章減浮折，覈中飽，民減納而賦增。

translations.literal: Bingzhang reduced inflated surcharges, audited middlemen's padding, so the people paid less while revenue increased.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang cut inflated surcharges and audited graft; taxpayers paid less while the treasury collected more.

sentences.zh: 仿揚州例，抽收鹽貨釐金，歲入百數十萬，給軍無缺。

translations.literal: Following the Yangzhou precedent, he levied a transit tax on salt goods, with annual intake of more than a million taels, supplying the army without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Yangzhou model, he levied a transit tax on salt, bringing in well over a million taels a year and keeping the armies supplied.

sentences.zh: 王珍戰江西，屢破悍寇，克樂安，尋卒於軍，以張運蘭及珍弟開化分統其眾。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen fought in Jiangxi, repeatedly defeated fierce rebels, took Le'an, and soon died in camp; Zhang Yunlan and Wang's younger brother Kaihua divided command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen fought in Jiangxi, repeatedly defeated tough rebel bands, captured Le'an, and soon died in the field; Zhang Yunlan and Wang's younger brother Kaihua split command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑攻臨江，至十二月克之。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou attacked Linjiang and took it by the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou besieged Linjiang and captured it in December.

sentences.zh: 八年，京察敘功，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, at the metropolitan performance review for recording merit, he was given the first-rank official's hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, at the capital performance review, he was awarded the first-rank official's hat ornament for merit.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑以疾歸，以劉坤一代領其軍。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou returned home on account of illness, and Liu Kunyi took command of his army in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou went home ill, and Liu Kunyi took over his command.

sentences.zh: 進規撫州、建昌，先後克復。

translations.literal: They advanced to recover Fuzhou and Jianchang, which were taken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to retake Fuzhou and Jianchang, recovering both in turn.

sentences.zh: 八月，諸軍齊集，克吉安。

translations.literal: In the eighth month all armies gathered and Ji'an was taken.
translations.idiomatic: In August the combined forces took Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 石達開敗竄浙江，江西略定。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai was defeated and fled into Zhejiang, and Jiangxi was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai was beaten and fled into Zhejiang, and Jiangxi was largely secured.

sentences.zh: 秉章以兵合不易，應乘勝進取。

translations.literal: Bingzhang held that concentrating troops was not easy and that they should press the advantage and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang argued that massing armies was difficult and that they ought to strike while victory was fresh.

sentences.zh: 疏請起曾國籓督師援浙，留蕭啟江、張運蘭兩軍隨徵，餘軍盡撤。

translations.literal: In a memorial he asked that Zeng Guofan be recalled to command the army aiding Zhejiang, keeping Xiao Qijiang's and Zhang Yunlan's two forces for the campaign while withdrawing all other troops.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne to recall Zeng Guofan to command the relief of Zhejiang, retaining only Xiao Qijiang's and Zhang Yunlan's corps for the expedition and pulling back the rest.

sentences.zh: 蓋自五年援江西，糜湖南餉凡二百六十萬，協濟之數不預焉。

translations.literal: For since aiding Jiangxi in the fifth year, Hunan's pay supplied had totaled 2.6 million taels, not counting coordinated subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fifth year of the war, Hunan had poured 2.6 million taels into the Jiangxi campaign alone, apart from coordinated subsidies from other provinces.

sentences.zh: 石達開由浙入閩、粵，徘徊五嶺之上。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai entered Fujian and Guangdong from Zhejiang and lingered atop the Five Ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai marched from Zhejiang into Fujian and Guangdong and hovered along the Five Ridges.

sentences.zh: 九年春，復由江西入湖南。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he again entered Hunan from Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1859 he invaded Hunan again from Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 秉章調魏喻義、陳士傑扼巋河，起劉長佑於家，令與劉坤一募勇四萬備迎擊。

translations.literal: Bingzhang shifted Wei Yuyi and Chen Shijie to hold the Kui River, recalled Liu Changyou from retirement, and ordered him with Liu Kunyi to raise forty thousand braves to meet the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang posted Wei Yuyi and Chen Shijie on the Kui River, called Liu Changyou out of retirement, and had him and Liu Kunyi recruit forty thousand militia to intercept the rebels.

sentences.zh: 調蕭啟江、張運蘭於江西，調田興恕於貴州，未集而賊至，陷桂陽​​、宜章、興寧，窺衡州，為巋河之軍所扼，回竄嘉禾、新田、臨武、寧遠。

translations.literal: He shifted Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan to Jiangxi and Tian Xingshu to Guizhou; before they had gathered the rebels arrived, took Guiyang, Yizhang, and Xingning, eyed Hengzhou, were blocked by the Kui River force, and fled back through Jiahe, Xintian, Linwu, and Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He redeployed Xiao Qijiang and Zhang Yunlan to Jiangxi and Tian Xingshu to Guizhou, but the rebels struck before the columns assembled, seized Guiyang, Yizhang, and Xingning, threatened Hengzhou, were checked at the Kui River, and doubled back through Jiahe, Xintian, Linwu, and Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 達開大隊竄永興，以據上游。

translations.literal: Dakai's main body fled to Yongxing to hold the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai led his main force into Yongxing to secure the upper river line.

sentences.zh: 劉長佑出祁陽，與之相持。

translations.literal: Liu Changyou came out of Qiyang and faced them in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changyou marched from Qiyang and locked horns with them.

sentences.zh: 回犯東安、新寧，劉坤一再挫之，乃趨寶慶，眾號三十萬，多烏合。

translations.literal: They turned to strike Dong'an and Xinning; Liu Kunyi defeated them twice, so they pressed toward Baoqing, their host claiming three hundred thousand, mostly a rabble.
translations.idiomatic: They swung against Dong'an and Xinning; Liu Kunyi beat them twice, and they then bore down on Baoqing with a host said to number three hundred thousand, most of them a disorderly mob.

sentences.zh: 秉章下免死令，散數万人。

translations.literal: Bingzhang issued an order sparing death, and dispersed tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang proclaimed an amnesty and dispersed tens of thousands of them.

sentences.zh: 時趙煥聯、田興恕等軍先至，營城外。

translations.literal: By then the armies of Zhao Huanlian, Tian Xingshu, and others had arrived first and camped outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhao Huanlian, Tian Xingshu, and other columns had already arrived and encamped outside the city.

sentences.zh: 賊營環二百里，包諸軍於中。

translations.literal: The rebel camps ringed two hundred li and wrapped the government armies within.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel camps stretched two hundred li around the field and hemmed the imperial forces inside.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼遣李續宜率軍赴援，秉章令劉長佑、劉岳昭、何紹彩分三路進。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi sent Li Xuyi leading troops to the relief; Bingzhang ordered Liu Changyou, Liu Yuezhao, and He Shaocai to advance in three columns.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi dispatched Li Xuyi with reinforcements, and Bingzhang sent Liu Changyou, Liu Yuezhao, and He Shaocai forward in three divisions.

sentences.zh: 六月，戰寶慶城下，內外夾擊。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they fought below Baoqing city, striking from within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In June they fought under the walls of Baoqing, attacking from inside and outside at once.

sentences.zh: 賊人眾乏食，再戰再敗，遂東竄。

translations.literal: The rebels were many but short of food; they fought twice and were twice defeated, then fled east.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were numerous but starving; beaten twice in succession, they broke eastward.

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江軍遇於永州，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: Xiao Qijiang's army met them at Yongzhou and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qijiang intercepted them at Yongzhou and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 乃由全州竄廣西，啟江尾追，劉長佑繼進，敗之於大榕口，又敗之桂林，賊竄慶遠。

translations.literal: They then fled through Quanzhou into Guangxi; Qijiang pursued their rear, Liu Changyou followed on, defeated them at Darongkou, defeated them again at Guilin, and the rebels fled to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They bolted through Quanzhou into Guangxi; Qijiang harried their rear while Liu Changyou pressed after, crushing them at Darongkou and again at Guilin until they fled toward Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 秉章令長佑留鎮廣西，田興恕回貴州，蕭啟江出沅江，兼顧川、黔。

translations.literal: Bingzhang ordered Changyou to remain garrisoning Guangxi, Tian Xingshu to return to Guizhou, and Xiao Qijiang to go out on the Yuan River, also watching Sichuan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang left Changyou to hold Guangxi, sent Tian Xingshu back to Guizhou, and sent Xiao Qijiang down the Yuan River to cover Sichuan and Guizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 時廣東賊又擾邊境，令張運蘭、黃淳熙分擊於江華、宜章，並殲之。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong rebels were again harassing the border; he ordered Zhang Yunlan and Huang Chunxi to strike them separately at Jianghua and Yizhang and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels were raiding the frontier again; he had Zhang Yunlan and Huang Chunxi hit them at Jianghua and Yizhang and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 十年，命赴四川督辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to Sichuan to supervise military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he was ordered to Sichuan to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時左宗棠已奉命募勇援浙，聘湘鄉劉蓉贊軍事。

translations.literal: At the time Zuo Zongtang had already been ordered to raise braves to aid Zhejiang and had engaged Liu Rong of Xiangxiang to assist in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang had already been commissioned to raise troops for Zhejiang and had hired Liu Rong of Xiangxiang as his military adviser.

sentences.zh: 湘軍名將多從曾國籓、胡林翼，惟劉岳昭、黃淳熙在湖南。

translations.literal: Most famed generals of the Hunan Army followed Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi; only Liu Yuezhao and Huang Chunxi remained in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Hunan Army's star commanders served under Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi; only Liu Yuezhao and Huang Chunxi were still in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 調兩軍隨行，受代將發，石達開復由廣東犯湖南境，吏民乞留。

translations.literal: He transferred the two armies to accompany him; just as the replacement general was about to set out, Shi Dakai again invaded Hunan's border from Guangdong, and officials and people begged him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: He called both corps to march with him, but as his successor was preparing to depart Shi Dakai again crossed into Hunan from Guangdong, and officials and commoners pleaded that he remain.

sentences.zh: 遣岳昭、淳熙會剿，賊尋引去。

translations.literal: He sent Yuezhao and Chunxi to join in suppression, and the rebels soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yuezhao and Chunxi to pursue them, and the rebels soon pulled back.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，始啟行，抵宜昌，聞陳玉成犯湖北，分遣岳昭赴援，自率五千人入川。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year he finally set out, reached Yichang, heard Chen Yucheng was invading Hubei, sent Yuezhao to the relief, and himself led five thousand men into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1861 he at last departed, reached Yichang, learned that Chen Yucheng was attacking Hubei, detached Yuezhao to reinforce there, and entered Sichuan with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 四川之亂，始於咸豐九年。

translations.literal: Sichuan's disorders began in the ninth year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The turmoil in Sichuan began in 1859.

sentences.zh: 滇匪藍大順又名朝柱，李短搭又名永和。

translations.literal: Yunnan bandits Lan Dashun, also called Chaozhu, and Li Duanda, also called Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Yunnan rebels were Lan Dashun, also known as Lan Chaozhu, and Li Duanda, also known as Li Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 結黨私販鴉片，其黨被捕，聚眾陷宜賓，攻敘州，擾嘉定，眾號十餘萬，群盜遂四起。

translations.literal: They formed a party to smuggle opium privately; when their fellows were arrested they gathered a crowd, took Yibin, attacked Xuzhou, and disturbed Jiading; their host claimed more than a hundred thousand, and bandits rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: They organized to traffic opium illicitly; when members were arrested they rose in arms, seized Yibin, struck at Xuzhou, and ravaged Jiading until their following was said to exceed a hundred thousand and brigands flared up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 總督有鳳、曾望顏等不能制，徵兵湖南，先遣蕭啟江一軍赴之。

translations.literal: Governors-general You Feng, Zeng Wangyan, and others could not control them and called for troops from Hunan, first sending Xiao Qijiang's corps.
translations.idiomatic: Governors-general You Feng and Zeng Wangyan could not contain them and requisitioned Hunan troops, dispatching Xiao Qijiang's force first.

sentences.zh: 啟江尋病歿，詔曾國籓赴川督師，中止未行，成都將軍崇實署總督。

translations.literal: Qijiang soon fell ill and died; the court ordered Zeng Guofan to Sichuan to command the armies, but the move was halted before he marched, and the Chengdu General Chong Shi acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Qijiang soon fell ill and died; the court then ordered Zeng Guofan to command in Sichuan, but the appointment was suspended before he marched, and General Chong Shi of Chengdu served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 秉章奉命後，慮客軍易遭齮齕，猶觀望。

translations.literal: After Bingzhang received his orders he feared that outside armies would easily meet obstruction and still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bingzhang received his commission he worried that outside troops would meet local obstruction and held back.

sentences.zh: 崇實馳書促行，開誠迎候，發夔關稅以給軍，軍至，乃出望外。

translations.literal: Chong Shi wrote urging him to hurry, received him with open sincerity, released Kui Pass customs revenue to pay the army, and when the troops arrived the welcome exceeded expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Shi urged him forward by letter, welcomed him frankly, released Kui Pass customs receipts for the troops, and when the army arrived the reception surpassed all expectation.

sentences.zh: 時賊首李永和、卯得興踞青神，藍朝柱圍綿州，張第才、何國梁圍順慶，蹂躪四十餘縣，將逼成都。

translations.literal: At the time the rebel chiefs Li Yonghe and Mao Dexing held Qingshen, Lan Chaozhu besieged Mianzhou, Zhang Dicai and He Guoliang besieged Shunqing, ravaging more than forty counties and about to press on Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders Li Yonghe and Mao Dexing held Qingshen, Lan Chaozhu besieged Mianzhou, Zhang Dicai and He Guoliang besieged Shunqing, and more than forty counties lay wasted as the rebels closed on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 秉章至萬縣，即令黃淳熙援順慶，戰於定遠，陣斬何國梁，賊大敗。

translations.literal: When Bingzhang reached Wanxian he at once ordered Huang Chunxi to relieve Shunqing; they fought at Dingyuan, slew He Guoliang in battle, and the rebels were heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Wanxian, Bingzhang immediately sent Huang Chunxi to relieve Shunqing; at Dingyuan they killed He Guoliang in the line and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 追至潼川二郎場，中伏，淳熙陣亡，然賊驚湘軍勇銳，引去。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Erlangchang in Tongchuan they fell into an ambush and Chunxi died in battle, yet the rebels, startled by the Hunan Army's fierce sharpness, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit carried them to Erlangchang in Tongchuan, where they were ambushed and Chunxi fell, but the rebels, shaken by the Hunan troops' ferocity, pulled away.

sentences.zh: 秉章由順慶進駐潼川，令胡中和、蕭慶、何勝必率蕭啟江舊部，曾傳理代領黃淳熙之眾，劉德謙率親軍，唐友耕率川軍，合萬九千人，援綿州，別以他軍綴青神，分扼東北。

translations.literal: Bingzhang advanced from Shunqing to garrison Tongchuan, ordered Hu Zhonghe, Xiao Qing, and He Sheng bi to lead Qijiang's old division, Zeng Chuanli to take Huang Chunxi's troops in his place, Liu Deqian to lead the personal guard, and Tang Yougeng to lead Sichuan troops—nineteen thousand in all—to relieve Mianzhou, while other forces pinned Qingshen and blocked the northeast in separate detachments.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang moved from Shunqing to Tongchuan, put Hu Zhonghe, Xiao Qing, and He Sheng bi at the head of Qijiang's veterans, had Zeng Chuanli replace Huang Chunxi's command, Liu Deqian lead the personal guard, and Tang Yougeng the Sichuan forces—nineteen thousand men in all—to relieve Mianzhou, while other columns held Qingshen and sealed the northeast.

sentences.zh: 會穆宗即位，擢授秉章四川總督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne Bingzhang was promoted to governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the accession of Emperor Muzong, Bingzhang was appointed governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，師會綿州城下，連破賊十餘壘，賊敗退，渡涪水屯守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the armies joined below Mianzhou city, broke more than ten rebel stockades in succession, the rebels were defeated and retreated, and crossed the Fu River to hold their ground.
translations.idiomatic: In August the combined forces met below Mianzhou, stormed more than ten rebel camps in turn, drove the enemy back across the Fu River, and penned them on the far bank.

sentences.zh: 官軍作五浮橋以濟，又擊敗之。

translations.literal: The government armies built five pontoon bridges to cross and defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops threw five pontoon bridges across the river and beat them again.

sentences.zh: 賊遁走，由什邡、崇慶趨丹棱，秉章始入成都。

translations.literal: The rebels fled by Shifang and Chongqing toward Danling, and Bingzhang at last entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled through Shifang and Chongqing toward Danling, and Bingzhang finally entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蒞任，奏劾布政使祥奎、中軍副將張定川不職，罷之。

translations.literal: On taking office he memorialized impeaching Provincial Administration Commissioner Xiang Kui and deputy commander Zhang Dingchuan for dereliction and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: Upon assuming office he impeached Administration Commissioner Xiang Kui and deputy commander Zhang Dingchuan for neglect and removed them.

sentences.zh: 薦劉蓉，詔超擢署布政使。

translations.literal: He recommended Liu Rong, and an edict promoted him by exception to acting administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Liu Rong, and the throne abruptly promoted him to acting administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 軍事吏治，振刷一新，於是分剿諸賊，急攻藍、李二股。

translations.literal: Military affairs and civil administration were thoroughly renewed, and then he divided forces to suppress the various bandits, pressing hard on the Lan and Li factions.
translations.idiomatic: He swept military and civil administration into fresh order, then split his forces against the scattered rebels and bore down on the Lan and Li factions.

sentences.zh: 令唐友耕扼眉州洪堰，斷青神之援，胡中和等諸軍圍丹棱，作長壕木城，節節進逼。

translations.literal: He ordered Tang Yougeng to hold Hongyan at Meizhou and cut Qingshen's relief, while Hu Zhonghe and the other armies besieged Danling, building long trenches and timber stockades and pressing step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yougeng was posted at Hongyan in Meizhou to sever Qingshen's support, while Hu Zhonghe and the other columns besieged Danling behind long trenches and timber forts, tightening the ring by stages.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城走，追斃藍朝鼎於陣。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned the city and fled; Lan Chaoding was pursued and killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned the city and ran; Lan Chaoding was run down and killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 餘賊分路逃散，為民團汛兵截殺幾盡。

translations.literal: The remaining rebels scattered along different routes and were nearly all cut down by militia and garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors scattered along several routes and were almost entirely cut down by local militia and garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 藍朝柱率二百人遁入山，尋出合諸匪陷新寧，復為官軍擊散。

translations.literal: Lan Chaozhu fled into the mountains with two hundred men, soon came out and joined various bandits to take Xinning, and was again dispersed by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Chaozhu escaped into the hills with two hundred followers, later re-emerged to join other brigands in seizing Xinning, and was scattered once more by government forces.

sentences.zh: 其後陝西盩厔匪潰走興安，為民團所獲，有自稱為藍大順及弟三順至九順，並戮之。

translations.literal: Later Zhouzhi bandits routed toward Xing'an were seized by militia; men claiming to be Lan Dashun and his brothers Third Dashun through Ninth Dashun were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, brigands routed from Zhouzhi toward Xing'an were caught by militia; men who called themselves Lan Dashun and his brothers Third through Ninth Dashun were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 李永和見丹棱已克，亦遁走，分軍追擊，圍之於鐵山。

translations.literal: Seeing Danling already taken, Li Yonghe also fled; forces were divided to pursue and surrounded him at Tieshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Danling fell Li Yonghe fled as well; detachments pursued and trapped him at Tieshan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，京察，詔嘉秉章殄寇迅速，整頓地方，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, at the metropolitan performance review, an edict praised Bingzhang for swiftly exterminating bandits and restoring order to the region and added Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, at the capital review of officials, an edict commended Bingzhang for quickly crushing the rebels and restoring local order and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋克青神，李永和、卯得興由鐵山遁走，追至宜賓，擒之。

translations.literal: Soon Qingshen was taken; Li Yonghe and Mao Dexing fled from Tieshan, were pursued to Yibin, and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshen was soon recovered; Li Yonghe and Mao Dexing broke out of Tieshan, were chased to Yibin, and captured.

sentences.zh: 道員張由庚克新寧，賊分竄，張第才遁陝西，曹燦章入老林。

translations.literal: Circuit Intendant Zhang Yougeng took Xinning; the rebels split and fled, Zhang Dicai escaped into Shaanxi, and Cao Canzhang entered the deep forest.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendant Zhang Yougeng recovered Xinning; the rebels scattered, Zhang Dicai slipped into Shaanxi, and Cao Canzhang vanished into the old-growth forests.

sentences.zh: 總兵周達武解涪州圍，追擒周紹湧於大竹，又擒郭刀刀於巴州。

translations.literal: Brigade-general Zhou Dawu lifted the siege of Fuzhou, pursued and captured Zhou Shaoyong at Dazhu, and also captured Guo Daodao at Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade general Zhou Dawu relieved Fuzhou, ran down Zhou Shaoyong at Dazhu, and seized Guo Daodao at Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 周毚毚由雲南入岳池、合州、新寧，張由庚擊走之，諸城皆复。

translations.literal: Zhou Chanchan entered from Yunnan into Yuechi, Hezhou, and Xinning; Zhang Yougeng drove him off and every city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chanchan crossed from Yunnan into Yuechi, Hezhou, and Xinning; Zhang Yougeng beat him back and the cities were all restored.

sentences.zh: 至冬，川南北一律肅清，詔嘉調度有方，予優敘。

translations.literal: By winter north and south Sichuan were uniformly pacified; an edict praised his able coordination and granted preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the province was quiet north and south; an edict praised his coordination and granted him preferential honors.

sentences.zh: 石達開見川中兵事方殷，屢由黔、楚窺伺來犯。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai, seeing Sichuan's military affairs still pressing, repeatedly peered in from Guizhou and Huguang to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai, noting that Sichuan was still fully engaged, repeatedly probed the borders from Guizhou and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 是年春，陷石柱，撲涪州，為劉岳昭軍所阻，竄黔境。

translations.literal: That spring he took Shizhu, struck at Fuzhou, was blocked by Liu Yuezhao's army, and fled into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That spring he seized Shizhu and lunged at Fuzhou, was checked by Liu Yuezhao, and bolted into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋又入敘永，攻江安，陷長寧，分擾珙、高、慶符，劉岳昭、曾傳理等擊敗之。

translations.literal: Soon he again entered Xuyong, attacked Jiang'an, took Changning, and raided Gong, Gao, and Qingfu; Liu Yuezhao, Zeng Chuanli, and others defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon re-entered Xuyong, struck Jiang'an, captured Changning, and raided Gong, Gao, and Qingfu before Liu Yuezhao, Zeng Chuanli, and others drove him off.

sentences.zh: 退滇境，分竄筠連、高縣，官軍扼金沙江以守。

translations.literal: He retreated into Yunnan and split to flee through Junlian and Gaoxian; government troops held the Jinsha River in defense.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew into Yunnan and split his force through Junlian and Gaoxian while government troops guarded the Jinsha River line.

sentences.zh: 賊謀三路入川，秉章調諸將及土司兵分防。

translations.literal: The rebels planned a three-route entry into Sichuan; Bingzhang shifted generals and native chieftain troops to guard each route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels aimed to enter Sichuan in three columns; Bingzhang redeployed his generals and native levies to block each approach.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，賴裕新自寧遠犯冕寧，至越巂，為工卩部土司嶺承恩擊斃。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Lai Yuxin invaded Mianning from Ningyuan as far as Yuexi and was killed in battle by Gongbu tribe chieftain Ling Chengen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1863 Lai Yuxin marched from Ningyuan against Mianning as far as Yuexi and was slain by Ling Chengen, chieftain of the Gongbu tribe.

sentences.zh: 餘賊散擾川西十餘縣，多為官軍民團截殺，盡殲於平武山谷中。

translations.literal: The remaining rebels scattered to harass more than ten counties in western Sichuan, were mostly cut down by government troops and militia, and were wholly destroyed in the Pingwu valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors raided a dozen western counties but were largely cut down by troops and militia and finally wiped out in the Pingwu ravines.

sentences.zh: 三月，石達開渡金沙江，為唐友耕等軍所扼，由小徑趨土司紫打地。

translations.literal: In the third month Shi Dakai crossed the Jinsha River, was blocked by Tang Yougeng and other armies, and took a bypath toward the native district of Zidade.
translations.idiomatic: In March Shi Dakai crossed the Jinsha River, was checked by Tang Yougeng and others, and turned onto a mountain track toward the native territory of Zidade.

sentences.zh: 大渡河水漲，官軍伺半濟擊之，退撲松林、小河，又為土司王應元所扼。

translations.literal: The Dadu River rose in flood; government troops waited until the rebels were half across and struck; driven back they rushed Songlin and Xiaohe and were again blocked by native chieftain Wang Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu was in flood; imperial troops hit them mid-crossing, and when they fell back toward Songlin and Xiaohe they were stopped again by the native chieftain Wang Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 嶺承恩夜襲破馬鞍山賊營，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Ling Chengen raided by night and broke the rebel camp at Ma'anshan, cutting their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Chengen attacked by night, smashed the rebel camp at Ma'anshan, and severed their supply line.

sentences.zh: 复連撲兩河，皆不得渡，糧盡，殺馬采樹葉而食。

translations.literal: They again pressed the two rivers but could not cross; provisions were exhausted and they killed horses and ate tree leaves for food.
translations.idiomatic: They tried both river crossings again and failed; with food gone they slaughtered their horses and ate leaves to survive.

sentences.zh: 唐友耕等漢、土官兵合擊，焚其巢，墮岩落水無數。

translations.literal: Tang Yougeng and other Han and native troops joined in attack, burned their nests, and countless fell from cliffs into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yougeng and combined Han and native forces stormed them, burned their encampments, and countless rebels plunged from the cliffs into the river.

sentences.zh: 餘七八千人奔老鴉漩，復為土兵所阻。

translations.literal: The remaining seven or eight thousand fled to Laoyaxuan and were again blocked by native soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight thousand survivors fled to Laoyaxuan and were hemmed in once more by native troops.

sentences.zh: 達開率一子及其黨三人乞降，解散四千人，餘黨盡誅之。

translations.literal: Dakai led one son and three of his partisans to beg surrender, disbanded four thousand men, and the rest of the party were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai came forward with one son and three lieutenants to surrender, released four thousand men, and the remainder were put to death.

sentences.zh: 五月，檻送達開至成都，磔於市。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Dakai was sent in a cage to Chengdu and dismembered in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In May Dakai was carted to Chengdu in a cage and executed by dismemberment in the public square.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔深嘉之，加太子太保，將士獎擢有差。

translations.literal: When the victory was reported an edict deeply commended him, added Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and rewarded officers and soldiers with differing promotions.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought an edict of high praise, the rank of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and graded promotions for the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 李福猷為達開死黨，初約由黔入川。

translations.literal: Li Fuyou was Dakai's die-hard partisan and had first agreed to enter Sichuan from Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuyou, a die-hard of Dakai's, had originally planned to enter Sichuan from Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 令劉岳昭與黔軍合剿，尋於黔境就殲。

translations.literal: Bingzhang ordered Liu Yuezhao to join Guizhou troops in joint suppression, and he was soon destroyed within Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang had Liu Yuezhao cooperate with Guizhou forces to exterminate him, and he was soon wiped out on Guizhou soil.

sentences.zh: 達開餘孽遂盡。

translations.literal: Dakai's remaining followers were thus completely ended.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Dakai's remaining followers were extinguished.

sentences.zh: 粵匪擾陝西，圍漢中，秉章令道員易佩紳率軍解其圍，張由庚駐防川境。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels harassed Shaanxi and besieged Hanzhong; Bingzhang ordered Circuit Intendant Yi Peishen to lead troops to lift the siege, with Zhang Yougeng garrisoning the Sichuan border.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong rebels raided Shaanxi and besieged Hanzhong; Bingzhang sent circuit intendant Yi Peishen to relieve the city and kept Zhang Yougeng on the Sichuan frontier.

sentences.zh: 至是復令蕭慶高、何勝必赴剿。

translations.literal: At this time he again ordered Xiao Qinggao and He Sheng bi to go for suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He now sent Xiao Qinggao and He Sheng bi to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔擢劉蓉為陝西巡撫，督諸軍。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Liu Rong to governor of Shaanxi to command the armies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict elevated Liu Rong to governor of Shaanxi to direct the forces.

sentences.zh: 秉章病目請告，命力疾視事。

translations.literal: Bingzhang, his eyes afflicted, asked leave; he was ordered to oversee affairs despite illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang, troubled by eye disease, requested leave but was told to carry on despite his ailment.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧克復，詔錄前後功，予一等輕車都尉世職，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangning was recovered; an edict recorded his past and present merit, granted the hereditary rank of First Class Commandant of Light Chariots, and bestowed the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when Nanjing fell, an edict tallied his services past and present, made him a first-class commandant of light chariots with hereditary right, and awarded the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 四年，陝西粵匪為諸軍擊敗，竄甘肅階州，令周達武會剿平之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Shaanxi's Guangdong rebels were defeated by the various armies and fled to Jiezhou in Gansu; Zhou Dawu was ordered to join in suppression and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 the Guangdong rebels in Shaanxi were beaten, fled to Jiezhou in Gansu, and were finally crushed in a joint campaign under Zhou Dawu.

sentences.zh: 回剿南坪番匪，匪首歐利哇降。

translations.literal: He then returned to suppress the Fan bandits of Nanping; the bandit chief Ou Liwa surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned back to the Fan rebels of Nanping, where the chief Ou Liwa submitted.

sentences.zh: 又剿馬邊，擒匪首宋士傑，邊境悉平。

translations.literal: He also suppressed Mabian, captured the bandit chief Song Shijie, and the borderlands were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Operations at Mabian brought the capture of Song Shijie, and the frontier was fully quieted.

sentences.zh: 令劉岳昭援黔，由綏陽抵遵義，道路始通，後由黔規滇，皆秉章遺策也。

translations.literal: He ordered Liu Yuezhao to aid Guizhou, reaching Zunyi by way of Suiyang so that the roads were open at last; later the advance from Guizhou toward Yunnan was also Bingzhang's legacy plan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Yuezhao to aid Guizhou, opening the road to Zunyi through Suiyang; the later push from Guizhou toward Yunnan likewise followed plans he had left behind.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，疾愈視事，命以四川總督協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year his illness eased and he resumed duties; he was ordered to serve as Grand Secretary while remaining governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1867 he recovered enough to resume office and was appointed a grand secretary while keeping the Sichuan governorship.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒於官，優詔賜卹，稱其「公忠誠亮，清正勤明」，贈太子太傅，入祀賢良祠，四川、湖南建專祠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died in office; a gracious edict granted funeral favors, praising him as "loyal, sincere, bright, and upright, pure, clear, diligent, and discerning," posthumously making him Grand Tutor, enshrining him in the Hall of Worthies, and building dedicated temples in Sichuan and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In November he died in office; the throne granted generous mourning honors and praised him as "loyal, sincere, bright, and upright; pure, clear, diligent, and discerning," posthumously raising him to Grand Tutor, enrolling him in the Hall of Worthies, and ordering temples in his name in Sichuan and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 賜其子天保郎中、天詒舉人，諸孫並賜官，諡文忠。

translations.literal: His sons Tianbao were made a director in the Secretariat and Tianyi a provincial graduate; all grandsons were also granted office; his posthumous title was Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianbao was made a secretariat director and Tianyi a provincial graduate; grandsons received offices as well, and his posthumous name was Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 秉章晚年愈負重望，朝廷要政多諮決，西南軍事胥倚之。

translations.literal: In his later years Bingzhang bore ever greater weight of reputation; many important policies of the court were referred to him for decision, and southwestern military affairs all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Bingzhang's standing only grew; the court consulted him on weighty policy, and the armies of the southwest looked to him for direction.

sentences.zh: 所論薦人才，悉被任用，著勳名。

translations.literal: The men of talent he recommended and discussed were all employed and won merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Every man of talent he recommended was taken up and went on to earn distinction.

sentences.zh: 川民感其削平寇亂，出於水火，及其歿，巷哭罷市。

translations.literal: The people of Sichuan were grateful that he had ended the ravages of banditry and lifted them from fire and water; when he died the lanes wept and markets closed.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's people credited him with ending the chaos that had drowned them in misery; at his death alleys filled with mourning and shops shut their doors.

sentences.zh: 遺愛之深，世與漢諸葛亮、唐韋皋並稱云。

translations.literal: The depth of his enduring love is spoken of in the same breath with Zhuge Liang of Han and Wei Gao of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The affection he left behind is still ranked with Zhuge Liang of Han and Wei Gao of Tang.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼，字潤之，湖南益陽人。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi, courtesy name Runzhi, was a native of Yiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi, styled Runzhi, came from Yiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父達源，嘉慶二十四年一甲三名進士，官至少詹事，學宗宋儒。

translations.literal: His father Dayuan, a third-rank graduate of the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, rose to Junior Mentor, and his learning followed the Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hu Dayuan had placed third in the palace examination in 1819, rose to junior mentor, and taught the Song Neo-Confucian masters.

sentences.zh: 林翼少時，即授以性理諸書，而林翼負才不羈，娶總督陶澍女，習聞緒論，有經世志。

translations.literal: In Linyi's youth he was already given the books on nature and principle, yet Linyi was talented and unrestrained; he married Governor-General Tao Shu's daughter, grew accustomed to great affairs in council, and harbored a will to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Linyi was drilled in Neo-Confucian moral philosophy, yet he was gifted and unruly; marriage to Tao Shu's daughter steeped him in high policy and fed his ambition to remake the world.

sentences.zh: 道光十六年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1836 he earned his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十年，充江南副考官，坐失察正考官文慶攜舉人熊少牧入闈，降一級調用。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he served as associate examiner for Jiangnan, and for failure to detect that chief examiner Wen Qing had brought in graduate Xiong Shaomu to the examination hall he was demoted one rank and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840 he served as associate examiner for the Jiangnan region and was demoted one rank for not catching chief examiner Wen Qing smuggling candidate Xiong Shaomu into the hall.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，捐納內閣中書，改貴州知府。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death, when mourning ended he purchased appointment as a Hanlin academy secretary and was changed to prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and the mourning period he bought a secretariat post, then took appointment as prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 署安順、鎮遠，皆盜藪，用明戚繼光法練勇士，搜捕林箐，身與同甘苦。

translations.literal: Acting at Anshun and Zhenyuan, both were lairs of bandits; he used Ming general Qi Jiguang's method to train brave men, searched the forested ravines, and shared hardship with the troops in person.
translations.idiomatic: At Anshun and Zhenyuan, both notorious bandit country, he trained fighters by Qi Jiguang's methods, combed the wooded gullies himself, and shared the soldiers' hardships.

sentences.zh: 屢擒劇盜，靖苗氛，以功賜花翎。

translations.literal: He repeatedly captured fierce bandits, pacified Miao unrest, and for merit was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly seized notorious outlaws, quieted Miao disturbances, and earned the peacock feather for his service.

sentences.zh: 又因防剿新寧匪李沅發，以道員用。

translations.literal: He was also employed as a circuit intendant for defending and suppressing the Xinning bandit Li Yuanfa.
translations.idiomatic: He was later commissioned as a circuit intendant to guard against and suppress the Xinning rebel Li Yuanfa.

sentences.zh: 總督吳文鎔、巡撫喬用遷並薦堪大用。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Wensha and Governor Qiao Yongqian together recommended him as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Wensha and Governor Qiao Yongqian both recommended him as a man of outstanding capacity.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，補黎平，實行保甲團練，千五百餘寨，建碉樓四百餘座，嚴扼要隘，儲穀備城守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was posted to Liping, implemented baojia militia training, over fifteen hundred stockades, built more than four hundred blockhouses, strictly held strategic passes, and stored grain to prepare for city defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he took charge at Liping, organized baojia militia across more than fifteen hundred hamlets, erected over four hundred blockhouses, sealed the strategic passes, and stockpiled grain for a siege.

sentences.zh: 地鄰湘、桂，匪戢而民安。

translations.literal: The region bordered Hunan and Guangxi; bandits were subdued and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Near Hunan and Guangxi, banditry was subdued and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 三年，剿甕安榔匪，誅其魁。

translations.literal: In the third year he suppressed the Lang bandits of Weng'an and executed their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he crushed the Lang rebels of Weng'an and put their leader to death.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫張亮基、駱秉章兩次奏調，以貴州留不行。

translations.literal: Hunan governors Zhang Liangji and Luo Bingzhang twice memorialized to transfer him, but Guizhou retained him and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's governors Zhang Liangji and Luo Bingzhang twice sought to transfer him, but Guizhou kept him and he never left.

sentences.zh: 御史王發桂疏薦林翼剿匪成效，詔赴湖北委用。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Fagui in a memorial recommended Linyi's results in bandit suppression; an edict ordered him to proceed to Hubei for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Fagui memorialized praising Linyi's success against bandits, and the court ordered him to Hubei for service.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢貴東道，率黔勇千人行次通城，而總督吳文鎔戰歿黃州，遂進援武昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted circuit intendant of Eastern Guizhou, led a thousand Guizhou braves marching through Tongcheng, while Governor-General Wu Wensha died in battle at Huangzhou, so he advanced to aid Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he was made intendant of eastern Guizhou, led a thousand Guizhou troops toward Tongcheng, learned that Wu Wensha had fallen at Huangzhou, and marched to relieve Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 賊尋犯湖南，駱秉章調林翼回防，平安化土匪，擢四川按察使，尋調湖北。

translations.literal: The rebels soon invaded Hunan; Luo Bingzhang recalled Linyi to defend, pacified Anhua native bandits, promoted him provincial judicial commissioner of Sichuan, then soon transferred him to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck Hunan, Luo Bingzhang recalled him; he pacified the native bandits of Anhua, was made Sichuan's judicial commissioner, and was soon shifted to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓既克武昌，檄林翼與羅澤南會攻九江，屯湖口，破賊梅家洲。

translations.literal: After Zeng Guofan had taken Wuchang, he ordered Linyi and Luo Zinan to join in attacking Jiujiang, encamped at Hukou, and defeated the rebels at Meijiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zeng Guofan recovered Wuchang, he directed Linyi and Luo Zinan against Jiujiang; they encamped at Hukou and took the rebel position at Meijiazhou.

sentences.zh: 五年春，擢湖北布政使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he was promoted provincial administration commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1855 he was made Hubei's provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 總督楊霈師潰黃梅，林翼率所部回援武昌，別以副將王國才一軍隸之，未至，漢陽陷，會攻不克，屯沌口。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yang Fu's army was routed at Huangmei; Linyi led his forces back to aid Wuchang, and separately attached Vice Commander Wang Guocai's army to him; before they arrived Hanyang fell, the joint attack did not succeed, and they encamped at Zhuankou.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Yang Fu's army broke at Huangmei, Linyi hurried back to Wuchang and subordinated Wang Guocai's brigade; before they arrived Hanyang fell, the assault failed, and the army camped at Zhuankou.

sentences.zh: 武昌复陷，潛師渡江規武昌，為賊所圍，兵少食盡，退金口。

translations.literal: Wuchang fell again; he sent troops secretly across the river to aim at Wuchang, was surrounded by rebels, with few troops and depleted food, and retreated to Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang fell again; Linyi sent a covert force across the river toward the city, was encircled with scant supplies, and withdrew to Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 詔林翼署理湖北巡撫，楊霈奏令上扼漢川。

translations.literal: An edict made Linyi acting governor of Hubei; Yang Fu memorialized ordering him upstream to hold Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him acting governor of Hubei, while Yang Fu ordered him to block Hanchuan upriver.

sentences.zh: 林翼疏陳形勢，宜急攻武漢，方能內固荊襄，上俞之。

translations.literal: Linyi in a memorial set forth the situation: Wuhan should be attacked at once, only then could Jing and Xiang be secured within; the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi argued that only a swift assault on Wuhan could secure Jingzhou and Xiangyang; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時武、漢、黃、德四郡皆為賊踞，後路崇陽、通城多伏莽，公私赤立，兵餉皆絀。

translations.literal: At that time the four prefectures of Wu, Han, Huang, and De were all held by rebels; on the rear route Chongyang and Tongcheng had many lurking brigands; public and private stores were stripped bare, and military pay was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Wuchang, Hanyang, Huangzhou, and De'an; Chongyang and Tongcheng behind him seethed with ambushers; treasury and household alike were bare, and pay ran dry.

sentences.zh: 林翼馳書四出乞貸，發家穀給軍。

translations.literal: Linyi sent letters in all directions begging loans and released his family's grain to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi begged loans across the province and fed the troops from his own family's granaries.

sentences.zh: 添募兵勇，兼顧南北兩路，凡數十戰，時有克捷，亦屢瀕於危。

translations.literal: He added recruited braves, attended to both north and south routes, fought several dozen battles, at times won victories, and also repeatedly neared danger.
translations.idiomatic: He raised more troops, guarded both flanks, fought dozens of engagements, won some and more than once nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 七月，攻克漢口鎮，奪大別山賊卡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he took Hankou town and seized the rebel stockades on Dabie Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In July he recovered Hankou and seized the rebel forts on Dabie Mountain.

sentences.zh: 未幾，援賊由漢川至，焚漢口。

translations.literal: Before long relief rebels came from Hanchuan and burned Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebel reinforcements came down from Hanchuan and burned Hankou.

sentences.zh: 崇、通匪勾結武昌城賊，撲金口大營。

translations.literal: Chong and Tong bandits joined with Wuchang city rebels and stormed the great camp at Jinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits from Chongyang and Tongcheng combined with the Wuchang garrison and struck the main camp at Jinkou.

sentences.zh: 詔念林翼素善用兵，勉以重整散卒。

translations.literal: An edict, mindful that Linyi had always been skilled at war, exhorted him to reorganize the scattered troops.
translations.idiomatic: The throne, remembering his military talent, urged him to rally the broken ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋退奓山，餉絕兵潰，下部議處。

translations.literal: Soon he retreated to Zhashan; pay ran out and the army broke; the Ministry deliberated punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell back to Zhashan; supplies gave out, the army scattered, and the ministries moved to discipline him.

sentences.zh: 林翼移營大軍山，收集潰兵，駐新堤、嘉魚。

translations.literal: Linyi moved camp to Dajun Mountain, gathered the broken troops, and encamped at Xindi and Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Dajun Mountain, gathered the fugitives, and held Xindi and Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 水陸合萬人，半出新募，賊至常數万，軍中奪氣。

translations.literal: Land and water forces together ten thousand men, half newly recruited; rebels often came in tens of thousands, and morale in the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: His land and river force barely reached ten thousand, half of them raw recruits; rebels often came in the tens of thousands, and his men lost heart.

sentences.zh: 林翼鎮靜相持，以忠義激勵將士，始漸定。

translations.literal: Linyi calmly held on, inspired officers and soldiers with loyalty and righteousness, and gradually the force steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi held his ground with calm, rallied the troops on duty and honor, and slowly steadied the army.

sentences.zh: 奏調羅澤南由江西來援，連克通城、崇陽，林翼自往迎之於蒲圻。

translations.literal: He memorialized to transfer Luo Zinan from Jiangxi as reinforcement; they successively took Tongcheng and Chongyang; Linyi went in person to meet him at Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: He called Luo Zinan from Jiangxi; Tongcheng and Chongyang fell in turn, and Linyi rode out to meet him at Puqi.

sentences.zh: 合破援賊韋俊、石達開於咸寧，復其城。

translations.literal: Together they defeated relief rebels Wei Jun and Shi Dakai at Xianning and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Together they shattered Wei Jun and Shi Dakai's relief column at Xianning and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 乘勝進攻武昌，自率所部普承堯、唐訓方軍由中路，羅澤南當西路，楊岳斌以水師會金口，總督官文亦令都興阿率騎兵駐北岸。

translations.literal: Seizing victory they advanced on Wuchang: he himself led his division, Pu Chengyao and Tang Xunfang's armies by the center route, Luo Zinan held the west route, Yang Yuebin joined with the water force at Jinkou, and Governor-General Guan Wen also ordered Duxing'a to lead cavalry stationed on the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage they besieged Wuchang: Linyi led Pu Chengyao and Tang Xunfang up the center, Luo Zinan blocked the west, Yang Yuebin's fleet joined at Jinkou, and Guan Wen posted Duxing'a's cavalry on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 林翼和輯諸將，軍勢遂日振，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Linyi harmonized the generals, the army's momentum daily strengthened, and battle after battle was won.
