translations.idiomatic: Linyi smoothed relations among his commanders; the army's strength rose day by day and battle after battle went their way.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，羅澤南急攻城，傷於砲，驟卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Luo Zinan pressed the assault on the city, was wounded by artillery, and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1856 Luo Zinan, pressing the assault, was struck by cannon fire and died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 以李續賓代領其軍，攻戰不少輟。

translations.literal: Li Xubin was made to take command of his army in his place; attacks did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin took over his corps and the fighting never slackened.

sentences.zh: 石達開自咸寧敗後，竄江西，連陷數郡。

translations.literal: After Shi Dakai's defeat at Xianning he fled into Jiangxi and successively took several prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Routed at Xianning, Shi Dakai fled into Jiangxi and seized one prefecture after another.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓屢調羅澤南迴援，不克往。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan repeatedly ordered Luo Zinan to return in relief but he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan repeatedly called Luo Zinan back, but the siege could not spare him.

sentences.zh: 林翼分遣劉騰鴻、普承堯兩軍赴之。

translations.literal: Linyi detached Liu Tenghong's and Pu Chengyao's two armies to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi sent Liu Tenghong and Pu Chengyao with separate columns to aid Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 詔以武漢久不克，督戰急。

translations.literal: An edict, because Wuhan had long not been taken, urgently pressed the war.
translations.idiomatic: The court, impatient that Wuhan still stood, ordered the assault pressed.

sentences.zh: 林翼疏陳，略曰：「臣頓兵城下五月餘矣。

translations.literal: Linyi memorialized, in summary: "Your servant has halted the army below the city for more than five months already.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi wrote in reply, in part: "Your servant has camped beneath the walls for more than five months.

sentences.zh: 血肉之軀，日當砲石，傷亡水陸士卒三千餘，喪將領羅澤南、周得魁百餘人，李續賓中丸墮馬者數矣。

translations.literal: Flesh-and-blood bodies face cannon and stone daily; more than three thousand land and water troops killed and wounded; lost generals Luo Zinan, Zhou Dekui, and more than a hundred others; Li Xubin has been struck by shot and fallen from his horse several times.
translations.idiomatic: Men face shot and shell every day; over three thousand soldiers have been killed or wounded on land and water; Luo Zinan, Zhou Dekui, and more than a hundred other officers are dead; Li Xubin has been shot from his horse more than once.

sentences.zh: 夫兵易募而將難求，臣觀前史，李左車告韓信，以頓兵城下，情見事絀為戒。

translations.literal: Troops are easy to raise but generals hard to find; your servant reads the older histories: Li Zuoche warned Han Xin that halting the army below a city until one's situation is exposed and affairs are exhausted should be a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers are easy to recruit but generals are not; I read how Li Zuoche warned Han Xin that stalemates beneath city walls expose weakness and court disaster.

sentences.zh: 戰易攻難，自昔已然。

translations.literal: Battle is easy, assault is hard; it has been so since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Field battle is easy; taking a fortified city is hard, and always has been.

sentences.zh: 故臣自四月後乃禁仰攻，分兵咸、蒲以取義寧，四戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Therefore from the fourth month your servant forbade assaults from below, divided troops between Xianning and Puqi to take Yining, and all four battles were victories.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fourth month I have forbidden uphill assaults, sent columns through Xianning and Puqi to seize Yining, and won all four engagements.

sentences.zh: 分水師以清下游，直達​​九江。

translations.literal: He divided the water force to clear the lower reaches and reach Jiujiang directly.
translations.idiomatic: I detached the fleet to clear the lower Yangtze as far as Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 臣自率兵五千扼武昌南路，李續賓率六千三百扼洪山東，分剿北路。

translations.literal: Your servant personally led five thousand to hold the south road of Wuchang; Li Xubin led six thousand three hundred to hold east of Hongshan and divide in suppressing the north route.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the southern approach to Wuchang with five thousand men; Li Xubin blocks the eastern Hongshan with sixty-three hundred and clears the north road.

sentences.zh: 水師六營下駐沙口。

translations.literal: Six battalions of the water force descended to encamp at Shakou.
translations.idiomatic: Six river battalions are posted downstream at Shakou.

sentences.zh: 賊由九江、興國分路來援，臣豫撥三千餘人戰於百里之外。

translations.literal: Rebels from Jiujiang and Xingguo came in relief by separate routes; your servant had beforehand detailed more than three thousand to fight a hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Jiujiang and Xingguo advanced in separate columns; I had already sent more than three thousand men to meet them a hundred li off.

sentences.zh: 微臣之志，誓與兵事相終始。

translations.literal: This humble servant's resolve is to swear to see military affairs through from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: This humble servant is resolved to see the war through to the end.

sentences.zh: 萬一變生意外，決不敢退怯苟且，自取羞辱。

translations.literal: Should mishap arise by chance, I absolutely dare not retreat in cowardice or seek easy safety and bring shame on myself.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns against me, I will not retreat in cowardice or disgrace myself by clinging to safety.

sentences.zh: 」文宗覽奏，特慰勉之。

translations.literal: " The Xianfeng Emperor read the memorial and especially comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and sent him special encouragement.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊於武昌城外豹子澥等處增壘掘壕，林翼抽調諸軍擊之，遂於要隘掘壕困賊。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rebels outside Wuchang at Baozixie and other places raised ramparts and dug trenches; Linyi detached armies to strike them, then dug trenches at strategic passes to hem in the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In May the rebels fortified Baozixie and other points outside Wuchang; Linyi struck their works and then dug entrenchments at the key passes to pin them in.

sentences.zh: 賊屢撲，皆擊退。

translations.literal: Rebels repeatedly charged; all were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated rebel sorties were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 諜知九江賊古隆賢來援，已至樊口，先遣黨數千進踞葛店。

translations.literal: Spies learned that Jiujiang rebel Gu Longxian was coming in relief, had already reached Fankou, and first sent several thousand followers to seize Geidian in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that Gu Longxian was marching from Jiujiang; he had reached Fankou and sent several thousand men ahead to seize Geidian.

sentences.zh: 令蔣益澧率精銳​​迎擊，戰於葛店，大破賊，焚其舟。

translations.literal: He ordered Jiang Yisui to lead elite troops to meet the attack; they fought at Geidian, routed the rebels, and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jiang Yisui with picked troops to meet them at Geidian, broke them utterly, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 追至樊口，楊載福水師亦至，合擊，斃賊數千。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached Fankou; Yang Zaifu's water force also arrived, and in combined attack several thousand rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Fankou, where Yang Zaifu's flotilla joined; together they killed several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 攻克武昌縣城，遂渡江攻黃州。

translations.literal: They took Wuchang county seat and then crossed the river to attack Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They took Wuchang county and crossed the river toward Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 而石達開由江西竄江寧，复糾眾上犯，分數路。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shi Dakai fled from Jiangxi into Jiangning, again gathered forces to invade upward, and divided into several routes.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shi Dakai fled from Jiangxi toward Nanjing, rallied his force, and struck upstream on several roads.

sentences.zh: 七月，急調黃州軍回援。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Huangzhou army was urgently recalled for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In July he recalled the Huangzhou column.

sentences.zh: 賊由金牛趨葛店，古隆賢亦起應之。

translations.literal: Rebels advanced from Jinniu toward Geidian, and Gu Longxian also rose to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels drove from Jinniu toward Geidian, and Gu Longxian rose to join them.

sentences.zh: 林翼督水陸軍分禦，連戰於油坊嶺、魯家港、姚家嶺、窯灣、沙子嶺、小龜山，旬日內二十餘捷，擒斬無算，解散脅從萬餘，追奔百餘里，至華容，賊悉遁。

translations.literal: Linyi commanded land and water forces in divided defense, fought in succession at Youfangling, Lujiagang, Yaojialing, Yaowan, Shaziling, and Xiaoguishan; within ten days more than twenty victories, captured and beheaded beyond counting, dispersed more than ten thousand coerced followers, pursued a hundred-odd li to Huarong, and the rebels all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi divided his land and river forces to meet them, fighting at Youfangling, Lujiagang, and a string of other points; in ten days he won more than twenty engagements, killed and captured without count, released over ten thousand pressed men, pursued a hundred li to Huarong, and the rebels fled altogether.

sentences.zh: 九月，楊岳斌追賊至蘄州，焚其舟，直抵田家鎮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Yang Yuebin pursued rebels to Qizhou, burned their boats, and pressed straight to Tianjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: In September Yang Yuebin chased them to Qizhou, burned their boats, and drove as far as Tianjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 賊援既絕，添募陸勇五千，水師六營，為長圖計。

translations.literal: With rebel relief cut off, he added five thousand land braves and six battalions of the water force for a long encirclement plan.
translations.idiomatic: With reinforcements cut off, he raised five thousand infantry and six river battalions for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 十一月，諮會官文剋期大舉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he consulted with Guan Wen to fix a date for a major effort.
translations.idiomatic: In November he and Guan Wen agreed on a date for the general assault.

sentences.zh: 楊岳斌斷攔江鐵鎖，焚賊船盡。

translations.literal: Yang Yuebin severed the iron chain blocking the river and burned all the rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuebin cut the Yangtze iron chain and burned every rebel vessel.

sentences.zh: 賊傾城出撲，鏖戰三時，大敗狂奔，諸軍逐之，遂復武昌。

translations.literal: Rebels poured from the city in a charge; fierce battle lasted three hours; they were routed in headlong flight; the armies pursued and thus recovered Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hurled their full strength outward; after three hours of slaughter they broke and ran; the pursuing columns retook Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 擒賊酋古文新等，駢誅數百人，生降四千。

translations.literal: They captured rebel chiefs Gu Wenxin and others, executed several hundred in pairs, and four thousand surrendered alive.
translations.idiomatic: They seized chiefs including Gu Wenxin, executed hundreds in batches, and took four thousand prisoners alive.

sentences.zh: 同日官文亦克漢陽。

translations.literal: The same day Guan Wen also took Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Guan Wen recovered Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 詔實授林翼湖北巡撫，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: An edict formally appointed Linyi governor of Hubei and added the first-rank official's hat knob.
translations.idiomatic: The court confirmed Linyi as governor of Hubei and granted the first-rank official's hat knob.

sentences.zh: 遂分兵收復武昌縣、黃州府及興國、大冶、蘄水、蘄州、黃梅。

translations.literal: He then divided troops to recover Wuchang county, Huangzhou prefecture, and Xingguo, Daye, Qishui, Qizhou, and Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Columns then recovered Wuchang county, Huangzhou, and Xingguo, Daye, Qishui, Qizhou, and Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 令李續賓乘勝規九江，都興阿、楊岳斌、鮑超屯小池口，自駐武昌籌全局。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Xubin to ride the victory toward Jiujiang; Duxing'a, Yang Yuebin, and Bao Chao encamped at Xiaochikou; he himself stayed at Wuchang to plan the overall situation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Xubin on toward Jiujiang, posted Duxing'a, Yang Yuebin, and Bao Chao at Xiaochikou, and remained at Wuchang to direct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 上疏論軍事吏治，略曰：「湖北軍務不飭已久，無論賊之多寡強弱，聞警先驚，接仗即潰。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on military and civil government, in summary: "Hubei military affairs have long been undisciplined; regardless of whether rebels are many or few, strong or weak, at word of alarm they panic first and break at contact.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on war and administration, writing in part: "Hubei's armies have been lawless for years; rebels large or small find them panicking at the first alarm and routed at the first blow.

sentences.zh: 上下相蒙，恬不知恥。

translations.literal: Upper and lower deceive one another, calmly without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men deceive one another and feel no shame.

sentences.zh: 誤於使貪使詐，而實為貪詐所使。

translations.literal: Mistaken in employing the greedy and deceitful, they are in fact driven by greed and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: They thought to use the greedy and crafty, but are themselves used by greed and craft.

sentences.zh: 川、楚、河南勇目，招合無賴投效，以一報十，冒領口糧。

translations.literal: Sichuan, Huguang, and Henan militia leaders gather worthless men to enlist, report one as ten, and fraudulently draw rations.
translations.idiomatic: Militia leaders from Sichuan, Huguang, and Henan recruit riffraff, report one man as ten, and draw rations for phantoms.

sentences.zh: 交綏即敗，又顧之他。

translations.literal: On joining battle they are at once defeated, then look to other commands.
translations.idiomatic: They flee at contact, then enlist under another commander.

sentences.zh: 帑項至艱，徒飽無賴欲壑。

translations.literal: Treasury funds are extremely strained, only filling the bottomless maw of riffraff.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is squeezed dry merely to glut desperadoes.

sentences.zh: 遣散不得其方，又相聚為盜。

translations.literal: Disbandment is not done by proper methods, and they gather again as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When disbanded improperly they band together again as brigands.

sentences.zh: 近年湖北募勇之大患，綠營則怯懦若性，正額虛浮，軍政營制，蕩然無存。

translations.literal: In recent years the great calamity of Hubei's recruited braves; the Green Standard Army is cowardly as if by nature, nominal rolls are inflated, and military administration and camp regulations have vanished entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited braves are the plague of recent years; the Green Standard troops are cowards by habit, rolls are padded, and army discipline has ceased to exist.

sentences.zh: 此為兵事急應整頓之要。

translations.literal: This is the essential point in military affairs requiring urgent rectification.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first military reform to undertake.

sentences.zh: 自古用武之地，荊襄為南北關鍵，武漢為荊襄咽喉。

translations.literal: Since antiquity in battlegrounds, Jing and Xiang are the north-south key, and Wuhan is the throat of Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the Jing-Xiang region has been the pivot between north and south, and Wuhan its throat.

sentences.zh: 武漢有警，則鄰疆胥震。

translations.literal: When Wuhan has alarm, neighboring territories all tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm at Wuhan shakes every neighboring province.

sentences.zh: 四年之中，武昌三陷，漢陽四陷。

translations.literal: Within four years Wuchang fell three times, Hanyang four times.
translations.idiomatic: In four years Wuchang fell three times and Hanyang four.

sentences.zh: 東南數省，受害惟武漢為甚。

translations.literal: Among the several southeastern provinces, only Wuhan suffered most severely.
translations.idiomatic: Of the southeastern provinces none suffered like Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 夫善鬥者必扼其吭，善兵者必審其勢。

translations.literal: One who fights well must seize the throat; one who employs troops well must examine the situation.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled fighter seizes his foe's throat; a skilled commander reads the terrain.

sentences.zh: 今於武漢設重鎮，則水陸東征之師，恃為根本軍火米糧委輸不絕，傷痍疾病休養得所。

translations.literal: Now if a strong garrison is set at Wuhan, the eastward land and water armies may rely on it as base; firearms, grain, and transport of supplies will be unbroken; wounded and sick will have proper rest.
translations.idiomatic: A stronghold at Wuhan would give the eastern armies a base with steady arms, grain, and convoys, and a place to heal the wounded.

sentences.zh: 平吳之策，必先保鄂，明矣。

translations.literal: The strategy to pacify Wu must first secure E; it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify the lower Yangtze one must first hold Hubei: that much is plain.

sentences.zh: 保鄂必先固漢陽。

translations.literal: Securing E must first fortify Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: To hold Hubei one must first secure Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 湖北之失，在漢陽無備。

translations.literal: Hubei's losses lay in Hanyang having no defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei was lost because Hanyang stood unguarded.

sentences.zh: 下游小挫，賊遂長驅直入。

translations.literal: A small defeat downstream, and the rebels then drove deep in at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: A minor setback downstream let the rebels pour straight in.

sentences.zh: 應請於武漢設陸師八千，水師二千，日夜訓練。

translations.literal: It is requested that at Wuhan eight thousand land troops and two thousand water troops be set, trained day and night.
translations.idiomatic: I urge establishing eight thousand infantry and two thousand sailors at Wuhan with constant drill.

sentences.zh: 平時有藜藿不采之威，臨事有千里折沖之勢。

translations.literal: In peacetime they would have the awe of not even wild greens being picked; in action the power to break the foe at a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In peace they would deter brigands even from the roadside weeds; in war they could check an enemy a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 且東征之師，孤軍下剿，苦戰必傷，久役必疲。

translations.literal: Moreover the eastward armies, lone columns descending to suppress, hard fighting must wound, long service must weary.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern armies fight far from home; hard battle wears them down and long service exhausts them.

sentences.zh: 傷病之人，留於軍中，不但誤戰，亦且誤餉。

translations.literal: Wounded and sick kept in the army not only spoil battle but also spoil pay.
translations.idiomatic: Sick men left in the ranks harm both fighting power and the pay rolls.

sentences.zh: 若以武漢之防兵更番迭代，則士氣常新，軍行必利。

translations.literal: If Wuhan's garrison troops rotated in turns, morale would stay fresh and military progress would surely profit.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating Wuhan garrisons would keep morale fresh and the march easier.

sentences.zh: 此武漢宜急設防練之要。

translations.literal: This is the essential point that Wuhan should urgently set defenses and training.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Wuhan needs garrison and drill without delay.

sentences.zh: 湖北莠民從賊者多，兵勇搜捕，徒滋擾害。

translations.literal: In Hubei many wicked people followed the rebels; soldiers searching and capturing only increase harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Many Hubei riffraff joined the rebels; chasing them with troops only harasses the innocent.

sentences.zh: 惟有保甲清釐，族戶綑獻，分別斬釋。

translations.literal: Only through baojia clear investigation and clans binding and presenting offenders, distinguishing execution and release.
translations.idiomatic: Only baojia registers, family bonds, and binding offenders for judgment, sparing some and executing others, will serve.

sentences.zh: 然牧令不得其人，則法不能行。

translations.literal: Yet if district magistrates are not the right men, the law cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Without fit magistrates, the law cannot be enforced.

sentences.zh: 官吏之舉動，為士民所趨向；

translations.literal: Officials' conduct is what scholars and people trend toward;
translations.idiomatic: How officials act is what scholars and commoners follow;

sentences.zh: 紳士之舉動，又為愚民所趨向。

translations.literal: Gentry's conduct in turn is what simple folk trend toward.
translations.idiomatic: and how the gentry act is what simple folk imitate.

sentences.zh: 未有不養士而能致民，不察吏而能安民者。

translations.literal: There has never been one who could win the people without nurturing scholars, or pacify the people without inspecting officials.
translations.idiomatic: No one ever won the people without nurturing scholars, or kept them quiet without watching officials.

sentences.zh: 五年大熟，州縣乃或報災，六年大饑，州縣轉或徵賦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year a great harvest, yet districts and counties sometimes reported disaster; in the sixth year great famine, yet districts and counties instead sometimes levied taxes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 the harvest was abundant yet some counties reported disaster; in 1856 famine struck yet some still collected taxes.

sentences.zh: 以豐為歉，是病國計；

translations.literal: Calling abundance shortage is to afflict the state's accounts;
translations.idiomatic: Calling plenty famine cripples the treasury;

sentences.zh: 以歉為豐，是害民生，而終害於國計。

translations.literal: To treat scarcity as abundance is to harm the people's livelihood, and in the end harms state revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Calling lean years prosperous harms the people and, in the end, the treasury.

sentences.zh: 歉歲官吏私收蠲緩，實惠不及於民。

translations.literal: In lean years officials privately collected what should have been remitted or deferred; real benefit did not reach the people.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years officials pocketed tax relief that never reached the people.

sentences.zh: 有所謂挖徵、急公等名目，無一非蠹國病民。

translations.literal: There are so-called items like 'supplementary levy' and 'urgent public service'—not one fails to harm the state and afflict the people.
translations.idiomatic: Every fee called an 'extra levy' or 'urgent contribution' drains the state and burdens the people.

sentences.zh: 凡下與上交接之事，諉之幕友；

translations.literal: Whatever concerns dealings between subordinate and superior, he shifts to a private secretary;
translations.idiomatic: Business with superiors he palmed off on secretaries;

sentences.zh: 官與民交接之事，諉之門丁。

translations.literal: whatever concerns dealings between official and people, he shifts to gate attendants.
translations.idiomatic: dealings with the people he left to gatekeepers.

sentences.zh: 詞訟案牘，病在積壓；

translations.literal: Petitions and case documents—the illness lies in backlog;
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits rotted in backlog;

sentences.zh: 盜賊姦宄，弊在因循。

translations.literal: bandits and violators—the abuse lies in procrastination.
translations.idiomatic: theft and outrage festered while officials dithered.

sentences.zh: 州縣之小事，即百姓之大事，今日之小賊，即異日之大賊。

translations.literal: A small matter in a district or county is a great matter for the people; today's small thief is another day's great thief.
translations.idiomatic: What magistrates dismiss as trifles are calamities for commoners; today's petty thief is tomorrow's rebel chief.

sentences.zh: 厝火積薪，隱憂方大。

translations.literal: Fire laid on piled fuel—hidden worry is just growing great.
translations.idiomatic: It is fire heaped on kindling; the hidden danger grows by the day.

sentences.zh: 又如捐輸則有踩堂、贄見之費，牙帖則有勒索之費，釐金則有私設之費。

translations.literal: Again for donation quotas there are 'treading the hall' and presentation-gift fees; for broker licenses there are extortion fees; for likin there are privately instituted fees.
translations.idiomatic: Donation drives brought 'hall treading' and greeting gifts; license brokers extorted; likin offices levied off-the-books charges.

sentences.zh: 臣受事以來，迭次特參，在國自有刑章，在臣甘為怨府。

translations.literal: Since this subject received office, repeatedly memorializing impeachments—in the state there are statutes of their own; for this subject, willing to be a magnet of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking office I have impeached official after official; the court has its laws, and I accept whatever hatred follows.

sentences.zh: 惟思劾貪非難，求才為難。

translations.literal: Only thinking that impeaching the greedy is not hard; finding talent is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissing the corrupt is easy; finding able men is hard.

sentences.zh: 前者劾去，後者踵事，而巧避其名，弊將不可勝言。

translations.literal: Those impeached and removed, those after follow the practice, yet craftily avoid the name—the abuses will be beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Remove one man and the next does the same under another name; the abuses would be beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為必嚴禁官場應酬陋習，與群吏更始，崇尚敦樸，屏退浮華。

translations.literal: This subject foolishly holds that one must strictly forbid the bad habit of official social courtesies, make a fresh start with all clerks, esteem plain honesty, and dismiss flamboyance.
translations.idiomatic: I urge banning official banqueting, starting afresh with every clerk, honoring plain duty and driving out display.

sentences.zh: 行之數年，庶可改觀。

translations.literal: Carry it out several years, perhaps one may change the aspect.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the administration might look different.

sentences.zh: 目下州縣懸缺待人，請敕下部臣，暫勿拘臣文法資格。

translations.literal: At present districts and counties have vacant posts awaiting men; I beg the Emperor order the Board members temporarily not to be bound by this subject's literary qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: Many county posts stand empty; I ask the Board not to limit appointments by examination seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 此吏治急應整飭之要。

translations.literal: This is the essential point that official government urgently should be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the urgent heart of civil administration.

sentences.zh: 武漢甫經收復，人或以為已治已安，臣竊憂之。

translations.literal: Wuhan has only just been recovered; some may think it already governed and at peace—this subject privately worries.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhan has only just been retaken yet some call it settled; I am uneasy.

sentences.zh: 如以為治安，則前收復已二次矣。

translations.literal: If one thinks it secured, then earlier recovery had already happened twice.
translations.idiomatic: If we call this peace, remember we had 'recovered' it twice before.

sentences.zh: 況江西七府俱淪於賊，旁軼橫出，不僅九江、安慶為足慮也。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiangxi's seven prefectures all fell to rebels; flanking columns burst forth sideways—not only Jiujiang and Anqing merit concern.
translations.idiomatic: Seven Jiangxi prefectures lie in rebel hands and raiders strike from every flank—not only Jiujiang and Anqing should worry us.

sentences.zh: 未收復之前，事勢極難，文武尚有懼心；

translations.literal: Before recovery the situation was extremely hard; civil and military still had fear in their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Before recovery the crisis kept civil and military officials afraid;

sentences.zh: 收復之後，佈置尚易，而特恐文武均萌肆志。

translations.literal: after recovery deployment is still easy, yet I especially fear civil and military alike will sprout reckless wills.
translations.idiomatic: after recovery work is easier, but I fear both will grow reckless.

sentences.zh: 外省粉飾之習，久在聖明洞鑑。

translations.literal: The provincial habit of cosmetic embellishment has long been in the sage clarity's penetrating view.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has long seen through provincial window-dressing.

sentences.zh: 不揣愚昧，用以直陳。

translations.literal: Not measuring my foolishness, using this to speak straight.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive my bluntness; I speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered; the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne and won the Emperor's praise and assent.

sentences.zh: 於是裁浮勇，練新軍，蠲四十六州縣田賦以蘇民困。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut redundant braves, drilled new armies, and remitted land tax in forty-six districts and counties to revive the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded useless militia, trained new troops, and remitted land tax in forty-six counties to ease hardship.

sentences.zh: 設清查局，稽核全省倉庫盈虛之數；

translations.literal: He set up a verification bureau to audit the surplus and deficit of every granary warehouse in the province;
translations.idiomatic: A verification office audited every warehouse in the province;

sentences.zh: 設節義局，表彰死難官紳士女；

translations.literal: he set up a bureau of integrity to honor officials, gentry, and women who died loyal;
translations.idiomatic: a bureau of integrity honored officials, gentry, and women who died loyal;

sentences.zh: 設軍需局，以備東征餉械。

translations.literal: he set up a military supplies bureau to prepare rations and arms for the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: and a supply office stocked the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 嚴課吏治，糾劾文武數十人，推廉尚能，手書戒勉將吏如子弟。

translations.literal: He strictly graded official government, impeached several tens of civil and military men, promoted the incorruptible who prized ability, and by hand wrote admonitions to generals and officials as to sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened civil rule, impeached dozens of officers, elevated the honest and capable, and wrote personal admonitions to his commanders like letters to sons.

sentences.zh: 初，將吏頗構督、撫異同，下令曰：「敢再言北岸兵事吏事長短者，以造言論罪。

translations.literal: At first generals and officials often fabricated differences between governor-general and governor; he issued an order saying: "Whoever again speaks of the north bank's military or civil affairs as long or short, take as fabricating talk and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Early on his officers played the governor-general against the governor; he ordered: "Anyone who gossips again about northern shore armies or civil affairs will be punished for sedition.

sentences.zh: 」官文亦開誠相與，無掣肘。

translations.literal: " Guan Wen also opened sincerity mutual dealing, with no pulling elbows.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen met him openly and no longer hamstrung him.

sentences.zh: 軍政吏治，皆林翼主稿，林翼推美任過，督撫大和。

translations.literal: Military government and civil government were all Lin Yi's main drafts; Lin Yi pushed beauty and bore blame—governor-general and governor great harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi drafted military and civil policy, gave credit and took blame, and governor-general and governor worked in harmony.

sentences.zh: 湖北振興，實基於此。

translations.literal: Hubei's revival truly had its foundation in this.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's revival rested on that accord.

sentences.zh: 襄陽土匪猖獗，擾及河南境，令唐訓方等剿之。

translations.literal: Xiangyang bandits ran rampant, disturbing even Henan's border; he ordered Tang Xunfang and others to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ravaged Xiangyang and spilled into Henan; he sent Tang Xunfang to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 七年春，擒匪首高先二等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he captured bandit chiefs Gao Xian'er and others.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1857 he captured the bandit leader Gao Xian'er and others.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成由皖北上犯，諸軍不能禦。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng came from Anhui northward in violation; the various armies could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng drove north from Anhui and no army could stop him.

sentences.zh: 林翼赴黃州督師，賊眾十餘萬環踞巴河東。

translations.literal: Lin Yi went to Huangzhou to supervise the army; rebel forces of over a hundred thousand ringed and held east of Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi took command at Huangzhou while more than a hundred thousand rebels held the east bank of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 會水漲，林翼令毀三台河石橋，扼河而守。

translations.literal: It happened the water rose; Lin Yi ordered the stone bridges of Santai River destroyed and held the river's choke point in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When floods rose he destroyed the Santai River stone bridges and held the choke points.

sentences.zh: 潛師出迴龍山，遏賊上竄。

translations.literal: A hidden column came out at Huilong Mountain to block the rebels' upward dash.
translations.idiomatic: A hidden detachment marched from Huilongshan to block their upstream escape.

sentences.zh: 調李續宜率湖勇馳至，督諸軍合擊於孫家嘴、馬家河、月山，賊大敗遁走。

translations.literal: He transferred Li Xuyi to lead Hunan braves galloping to arrive, supervised the various armies in united attack at Sunjiazui, Majiahe, and Yueshan; the rebels were greatly defeated and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Li Xuyi with Hunan troops and led a joint assault at Sunjiazui, Majiahe, and Yueshan; the rebels were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 都興阿、李續賓亦連破賊於黃梅、宿松，楚北肅清。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a and Li Xubin also in succession broke rebels at Huangmei and Susong; northern Chu was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a and Li Xubin followed with victories at Huangmei and Susong, and northern Hubei was cleared.

sentences.zh: 遂視師九江，定合圍方略而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inspected the army at Jiujiang, fixed the united encirclement strategy, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then inspected forces at Jiujiang, set the encirclement plan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，李續賓等攻九江，克之，磔賊首林啟榮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year Li Xubin and others attacked Jiujiang and took it; the rebel chief Lin Qirong was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1858 Li Xubin took Jiujiang and had the rebel chief Lin Qirong executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉林翼調度有方，加太子少保。

translations.literal: An edict praised Lin Yi's dispatch and planning as having method; he was advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his command and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 林翼乃急規安慶，楊岳斌率水師出九江，都興阿出宿松、望江，逼安慶為圍師。

translations.literal: Lin Yi then urgently planned Anqing; Yang Yuebin led the water army out from Jiujiang, Du Xing'a out from Susong and Wangjiang, pressing Anqing as encircling troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi turned to Anqing: Yang Yuebin sailed from Jiujiang, Du Xing'a marched from Susong and Wangjiang, and both closed on the siege.

sentences.zh: 李續賓規复太湖、潛山、桐城，與都軍為犄角。

translations.literal: Li Xubin planned to recover Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng, forming a horn with Du's army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xubin aimed to retake Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng as a pincer with Du Xing'a.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁母憂，詔予假百日治喪，假滿仍署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he entered mourning for his mother; an edict granted leave of a hundred days to conduct the funeral; when leave ended he still acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In May he began mourning for his mother; the court gave him a hundred days' leave and ordered him back to the governorship when it ended.

sentences.zh: 七月，廬州陷，李續賓輕軍赴援，戰歿三河。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Luzhou fell; Li Xubin with a light force went to rescue and died in battle at Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: In July Luzhou fell; Li Xubin rushed with a light force and was killed at Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 林翼方奉母柩回籍，詔急起視師，林翼聞命，痛哭起行，迳次黃州，軍心始定。

translations.literal: Lin Yi was just escorting his mother's coffin back to his native place; an edict urgently recalled him to command the army; on hearing the order Lin Yi wept, arose, and traveled; he went straight to encamp at Huangzhou, and army hearts then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi was escorting his mother's coffin home when an urgent edict recalled him; he wept, rose, and marched straight to Huangzhou, steadying the armies.

sentences.zh: 九年，進屯上巴河，與李續宜整飭部伍，日夜訓練，謀大舉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he advanced and encamped at Shangbahe, with Li Xuyi rectifying and ordering the ranks, training day and night, planning a great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he encamped at Shangbahe, joined Li Xuyi in drilling the ranks night and day, and planned a major offensive.

sentences.zh: 會石達開由江西犯湖南，圍寶慶。

translations.literal: It happened Shi Dakai from Jiangxi violated Hunan and besieged Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai invaded Hunan from Jiangxi and besieged Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 林翼令李續宜率所部赴援，舒保馬隊助之，又以水師分扼河道，寶慶圍得解，於是與曾國籓合力圖復安徽。

translations.literal: Lin Yi ordered Li Xuyi to lead his division to rescue, Shu Bao's cavalry to assist, and also used the water army in sections to choke the river routes; the siege of Baoqing was released—thereupon with Zeng Guofan he united strength to plan recovering Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Xuyi with Shu Bao's cavalry and detachments of sailors to hold the rivers; Baoqing was relieved, and he joined Zeng Guofan to retake Anhui.

sentences.zh: 國籓循江而下為第一路，多隆阿、鮑超攻取潛山、太湖為第二路，林翼自出英山、霍山為第三路，李續宜由松子關出商城、固始為第四路。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan down the river was the first route; Duo Long'a and Bao Chao attacking to take Qianshan and Taihu was the second route; Lin Yi himself out from Yingshan and Huoshan was the third route; Li Xuyi from Songzi Pass out to Shangcheng and Gushi was the fourth route.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan would advance downriver as the first column; Duo Long'a and Bao Chao would take Qianshan and Taihu as the second; Lin Yi would march from Yingshan and Huoshan as the third; Li Xuyi would come through Songziguan toward Shangcheng and Gushi as the fourth.

sentences.zh: 十月，由黃州移營英山。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he moved camp from Huangzhou to Yingshan.
translations.idiomatic: In October he moved headquarters from Huangzhou to Yingshan.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成在賊中最狡悍，見太湖圍急，糾合捻匪張洛行、龔瞎子眾數十萬來援。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng among rebels was most cunning and fierce; seeing Taihu's siege urgent, he gathered Nian bandits Zhang Luoxing, Gong the Blind, and masses of several hundred thousand to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng, the rebels' craftiest commander, saw Taihu hard pressed and rallied the Nian leaders Zhang Luoxing and Gong the Blind with hundreds of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 林翼集諸軍精銳全力備戰，欲一鼓殲之。

translations.literal: Lin Yi gathered the various armies' elite strength in full to prepare battle, wishing in one drumbeat to annihilate them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi massed his best troops for a battle meant to destroy them in one blow.

sentences.zh: 與曾國籓部署諸將，指揮戰略。

translations.literal: With Zeng Guofan he deployed the generals and directed strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zeng Guofan deployed the generals and set strategy.

sentences.zh: 謀前敵總統，以多隆阿謀勇兼優，而鮑超素不相下，手書勸勉，十數往復，始定議。

translations.literal: They sought a front-line supreme commander; Duo Long'a had strategy and courage both excellent, yet Bao Chao by nature would not submit; by hand he wrote exhortations, a dozen or more exchanges back and forth, before the decision was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: They needed a field commander; Duo Long'a had both brains and nerve, but Bao Chao would not defer to him until Lin Yi exchanged a dozen personal letters of persuasion.

sentences.zh: 又備意外，令金國琛、-{余}-際昌以八千人出潛山天堂拊賊背。

translations.literal: Also preparing for contingencies, he ordered Jin Guochen and Yu Jichang with eight thousand men out from Qianshan's Tiantang to strike the rebels' rear.
translations.idiomatic: As insurance he sent Jin Guochen and Yu Jichang with eight thousand men through Qianshan's Tiantang to hit the enemy's rear.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊至，鮑超營小池驛，當其衝，賊聚攻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebels arrived; Bao Chao camped at Xiaochiyi, bore their rush, and the rebels massed to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In December the rebels arrived; Bao Chao held Xiaochiyi on the main road and they concentrated their assault on him.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿慮分兵掣全勢，置不救，調唐訓方往助。

translations.literal: Duo Long'a feared dividing troops would restrain the whole force's power, set it aside without rescue, and transferred Tang Xunfang to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Long'a feared splitting his force and held back, then sent Tang Xunfang to help.

sentences.zh: 事且急，金國琛等由山中鼓行而出，賊乃奪氣。

translations.literal: The affair was already urgent; Jin Guochen and others drum-marched out from the mountains, and the rebels then lost spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis peaked, Jin Guochen's men marched beating drums from the hills and the rebels' morale broke.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，多隆阿攻羅山沖為西路，鮑超出小池驛為東路，硃品隆、蔣凝學、唐訓方等合擊，金國琛等亦同時並進，大破賊，殲斃先後二萬餘，遂克太湖城，潛山亦復。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year Duo Long'a attacked Luoshanchong as the western route, Bao Chao out from Xiaochiyi as the eastern route; Zhu Pinlong, Jiang Ningxue, Tang Xunfang, and others struck together, Jin Guochen and others also advanced at the same time, greatly defeating the rebels and killing over twenty thousand in succession; thereupon Taihu city was taken and Qianshan also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1860 Duo Long'a struck Luoshanchong on the west and Bao Chao on the east at Xiaochiyi; Zhu Pinlong, Jiang Ningxue, Tang Xunfang, Jin Guochen, and others joined the assault, killing more than twenty thousand rebels and recovering Taihu and Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 是役為僅見之大捷，安慶之勢遂孤。

translations.literal: This campaign was a great victory rarely seen; Anqing's situation then stood isolated.
translations.idiomatic: It was a victory seldom matched in the war, and Anqing was left isolated.

sentences.zh: 既而江南大軍潰，蘇、常盡陷，曾國籓授兩江總督，督師。

translations.literal: Soon after the great armies of Jiangnan collapsed, Suzhou and Changzhou all fell; Zeng Guofan was appointed governor-general of Liangjiang and supervised the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Jiangnan armies collapsed and Suzhou and Changzhou fell; Zeng Guofan became governor-general of Liangjiang and took command.

sentences.zh: 林翼為畫分路大舉之策，國籓不盡用，率鮑超等次祁門，為規复江南計，以其弟國荃圍安慶。

translations.literal: Lin Yi for him drew a plan of divided routes for a great undertaking; Zeng Guofan did not fully use it, leading Bao Chao and others to encamp at Qimen as a plan to recover Jiangnan, with his younger brother Guoquan besieging Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi drafted a multi-pronged offensive; Zeng Guofan used only part of it, camping Bao Chao at Qimen to recover the lower Yangtze while his brother Guoquan besieged Anqing.

sentences.zh: 林翼令多隆阿圍桐城，李續宜屯青草塥，為兩軍援，都興阿別出師江北，分兵濟餉，林翼悉任之。

translations.literal: Lin Yi ordered Duo Long'a to besiege Tongcheng, Li Xuyi to encamp at Qingcaodi, as relief for the two armies; Du Xing'a separately led troops on the north bank, dividing forces to ferry supplies—Lin Yi entrusted all to them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi had Duo Long'a besiege Tongcheng and Li Xuyi hold Qingcaodi in support; Du Xing'a operated north of the river with divided columns for supplies, and Lin Yi left all of it to them.

sentences.zh: 十月，多隆阿、李續宜大破賊於桐城掛車河。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Duo Long'a and Li Xuyi greatly defeated rebels at Tongcheng's Guache River.
translations.idiomatic: In October Duo Long'a and Li Xuyi routed the rebels at Guache River near Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 林翼進駐太湖，度賊援安慶不利，必深入湖北腹地以分我軍勢。

translations.literal: Lin Yi advanced headquarters to Taihu, judging that aiding Anqing would be unfavorable for the rebels, who would surely deep-strike Hubei's interior to divide our army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi moved to Taihu, reasoning that if relief for Anqing failed the rebels would plunge into Hubei's heartland to split his forces.

sentences.zh: 令-{余}-際昌屯霍山樂兒嶺，成大吉屯羅田松子關，戒賊至勿浪戰，堅守待援。

translations.literal: He ordered Yu Jichang to encamp at Huoshan's Le'er Ridge, Cheng Daji at Luotian's Songzi Pass, warning that when rebels arrived they must not fight rashly but hold fast awaiting relief.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Yu Jichang at Le'erling in Huoshan and Cheng Daji at Songziguan in Luotian, ordering them not to offer reckless battle but to hold until reinforcements came.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，賊果合捻匪西犯，成大吉破之松子關，殲捻渠龔瞎子。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year the rebels indeed united with Nian bandits and violated westward; Cheng Daji broke them at Songzi Pass and killed the Nian chief Gong the Blind.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1861 the rebels joined Nian forces in a western drive; Cheng Daji defeated them at Songziguan and killed the Nian chief Gong the Blind.

sentences.zh: 霍山守者違節度，為賊所敗，遂進陷黃州、德安、孝感、隨州，林翼令李續宜回援。

translations.literal: Huoshan's defenders violated discipline and were defeated by rebels, who then advanced to seize Huangzhou, De'an, Xiaogan, and Suizhou; Lin Yi ordered Li Xuyi back to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Huoshan garrison disobeyed orders, was beaten, and the rebels took Huangzhou, De'an, Xiaogan, and Suizhou; Lin Yi recalled Li Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 賊復分股回略蘄、黃，趨安慶，約城賊夾擊。

translations.literal: The rebels again split columns to raid Qizhou and Huangzhou and hurry toward Anqing, arranging with the city rebels for a pincer strike.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel detachments swept back through Qizhou and Huangzhou toward Anqing to coordinate with the garrison in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 檄成大吉下援，鮑超亦由南岸至，破賊於集賢關，擒斬數千，磔其渠劉瑲林。

translations.literal: He ordered Cheng Daji down to aid; Bao Chao also arrived from the south bank, broke rebels at Jixian Pass, captured and killed several thousand, and dismembered their chief Liu Qilin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cheng Daji south; Bao Chao came up from the south bank, smashed the rebels at Jixian Pass, killed thousands, and executed their leader Liu Qilin by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿亦破援賊於桐城，賊計不得逞，城中糧將盡，勢益慼。

translations.literal: Duo Long'a also broke relief rebels at Tongcheng; the rebels' plan could not succeed, grain in the city was nearly exhausted, and their situation grew more desperate.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Long'a routed the relief force at Tongcheng; with their plan foiled and provisions inside Anqing nearly gone, the defenders grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 南岸之賊復由江西犯興國、大冶，南及崇、通，武漢震動。

translations.literal: South-bank rebels again from Jiangxi violated Xingguo and Daye, southward reaching Chongyang and Tongcheng; Wuhan was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels south of the river struck from Jiangxi into Xingguo and Daye and as far as Chongyang and Tongcheng, shaking Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 林翼方病咯血，自率師回援，而圍攻安慶益急。

translations.literal: Lin Yi was then ill, coughing blood, personally leading the army back to rescue, while the siege of Anqing grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Though ill and coughing blood, Lin Yi led troops back to rescue Hubei even as the siege of Anqing tightened.

sentences.zh: 及抵湖北，賊已聞風遁。

translations.literal: When he reached Hubei the rebels had already fled on hearing the news.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Hubei the rebels had fled at the news of his approach.

sentences.zh: 八月朔，遂克安慶。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month Anqing was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month Anqing fell.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓推林翼為首功，詔加太子太保，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan pushed Lin Yi as chief merit; an edict advanced him to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan credited Lin Yi as chief architect of victory; the throne made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted a hereditary commandant's rank.

sentences.zh: 桐城、廬江、舒城以次復，黃州、德安之賊先後擒斬，楚境悉平。

translations.literal: Tongcheng, Lujiang, and Shucheng were recovered in succession; Huangzhou and De'an rebels were captured and killed before and after; Chu territory was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng, Lujiang, and Shucheng were retaken; rebels in Huangzhou and De'an were hunted down; Hubei was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 林翼久病，聞文宗崩於熱河行在，大慟嘔血，八月，卒。

translations.literal: Lin Yi had long been ill; on hearing Emperor Wenzong died at the Rehe traveling palace he grieved greatly, vomited blood, and in the eighth month died.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill, he learned that Emperor Wenzong had died at Rehe, grieved until he vomited blood, and died in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 詔贈總督，祀賢良祠，湖北、湖南並建專祠，賜其子子勳舉人，諡文忠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him governor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, with dedicated temples in Hubei and Hunan; his son Ziqin was granted juren status; posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously honored him as governor, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, built temples in Hubei and Hunan, granted his son Ziqin the juren degree, and gave him the posthumous name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，复詔：「林翼未竟全功，遽就溘逝，跡其功勳卓越，名播寰區，至今江、鄂士民稱頌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict again said: "Lin Yi did not complete his full achievement but suddenly passed away; tracing his merit as outstanding, his name spread through the realm, and to this day scholars and people of the Jiang and E regions praise and chant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 the court declared: "Lin Yi died before finishing his work, yet his feats were supreme and his fame still fills the land; the people of the middle Yangtze and Hubei praise him to this day."

sentences.zh: 命於原籍家祠賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: " Order at his native-place family shrine the gift of one sacrifice altar.
translations.idiomatic: It ordered one imperial sacrifice at his ancestral hall in his home county.

sentences.zh: 」洎江南平，加予一等輕車都尉世職，子子勳襲，後併兩世職為男爵。

translations.literal: " When Jiangnan was pacified, added grant of first-class Light Chariot Commandant hereditary office; son Ziqin inherited; later the two hereditary offices were merged as baron.
translations.idiomatic: After the lower Yangtze was pacified he received an additional first-class Light Chariot Commandant hereditary rank, which his son Ziqin inherited and later merged with the earlier rank into a baronetcy.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，以孫祖廕襲，官郵傳部參議。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period his grandson Zuyin inherited, serving as a secretary in the Ministry of Posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu era his grandson Zuyin inherited the title and served as secretary in the Ministry of Posts.

sentences.zh: 林翼貌英偉，目岩岩，威棱懾人。

translations.literal: Lin Yi's appearance was heroic; his eyes stern as rocks; awe-inspiring edge deterred people.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi looked imposing, with a rock-steady gaze that awed those around him.

sentences.zh: 事至立斷，無留難。

translations.literal: When affairs arrived he decided at once, with no lingering difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: When business came he decided it on the spot without delay.

sentences.zh: 尤長綜覈，釐正湖北漕糧積弊，以部定漕折為率，因地量加輕重，民歲減錢百餘萬緡，歲增帑四十餘萬兩，提存節省銀亦三十餘萬兩。

translations.literal: He was especially good at comprehensive audit, rectifying accumulated abuses of Hubei's grain transport; using the Board's fixed grain conversion rate as standard, he measured additions light or heavy according to locality—the people yearly reduced cash by over a million strings, yearly increased treasury by over four hundred thousand taels, and saved silver set aside also over three hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at auditing accounts, reformed Hubei's corrupt grain-tax system on the basis of the Board rate, and adjusted surcharges by locality—cutting more than a million strings from the people's yearly burden, adding more than four hundred thousand taels to revenue, and banking over three hundred thousand taels in savings.

sentences.zh: 兩湖自淮鹽阻絕，率食川鹽，於宜昌、沙市、武穴、老河口設局徵稅，視舊課增至倍蓰。

translations.literal: The two lakes since Huai salt was cut off mostly ate Sichuan salt; at Yichang, Shashi, Wuxue, and Laohekou he set bureaus to levy tax, compared with the old levy increased to several times.
translations.idiomatic: With Huai salt cut off, Huguang lived on Sichuan salt; he taxed it at Yichang, Shashi, Wuxue, and Laohekou at several times the old rate.

sentences.zh: 時東南各省皆抽釐助餉，惟湖北多用士人司榷，覈實無弊。

translations.literal: At the time southeastern provinces all drew likin to aid military pay; only Hubei mostly used scholar-gentry to manage levies, verified in fact without abuse.
translations.idiomatic: While southeastern provinces used likin to fund armies, Hubei mostly put scholars in charge of collection and kept the levies honest.

sentences.zh: 其治軍務明紀律，手訂營制，留意將才。

translations.literal: His governing military affairs had clear discipline; he hand-drafted camp regulations and paid attention to general talent.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the army with strict discipline, wrote the regulations himself, and cultivated commanders.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「兵之囂者無不罷，將之貪者無不怯；

translations.literal: He once said: "Troops that clamor never fail to fail; generals that are greedy never fail to be timid;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Boisterous troops always fail; greedy generals always flinch;

sentences.zh: 觀將知兵，觀兵知將。

translations.literal: observe the general and you know the troops; observe the troops and you know the general.
translations.idiomatic: study the commander and you know the army, study the army and you know the commander.

sentences.zh: 為統將必明大體，知進退緩急機宜；

translations.literal: As supreme commander one must understand the great principle and know advance, retreat, urgency, and opportune timing;
translations.idiomatic: A supreme commander must grasp the big picture and know when to advance, retreat, or wait;

sentences.zh: 其次知陣法，臨敵決勝；

translations.literal: next know battle arrays and decide victory facing the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: next know formations and win in the field;

sentences.zh: 又其次勇敢：此大小之分也。

translations.literal: again next, bravery: this is the distinction of great and small.
translations.idiomatic: last comes mere bravery—that is the least of the three.

sentences.zh: 」馭將以誠，因材而造就之，多以功名顯。

translations.literal: " He commanded generals with sincerity, according to talent and cultivating them—many by merit and fame became illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: He led his officers with sincerity, shaped them to their gifts, and many rose to fame and rank.

sentences.zh: 察吏嚴而不沒一善，手書褒美，受者榮於薦剡，故文武皆樂為之用。

translations.literal: He inspected officials strictly yet never overlooked a single merit, personally wrote words of praise, and those who received them felt more honored than by a memorial of recommendation; therefore civil and military men alike were glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He scrutinized officials rigorously yet never let a good deed pass unnoticed, wrote personal letters of praise, and recipients felt more honored than by an official recommendation—so men of every rank were eager to serve him.

sentences.zh: 士有志節才名不樂仕進者，千里招致，於武昌立寶善堂居之，以示坊表。

translations.literal: Scholars of integrity and talent who did not wish to pursue office he summoned from a thousand li away, established the Baoshan Hall at Wuchang for them to dwell in, and thereby set an example for society.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and principle who shunned official careers he drew from afar, housed at the Baoshan Hall in Wuchang, and held up as models for others.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「國之需才，猶魚之需水，鳥之需林，人之需氣，草木之需土。

translations.literal: He once said: "A state's need for talent is like a fish's need for water, a bird's need for forest, a man's need for breath, or grass and trees' need for soil."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "A state needs talent the way fish need water, birds need forests, people need air, and plants need soil."

sentences.zh: 得之則生，不得則死。

translations.literal: Obtain it and one lives; fail to obtain it and one dies.
translations.idiomatic: With it they live; without it they perish.

sentences.zh: 才者無求於天下，天下當自求之。

translations.literal: Men of talent do not beg the world; the world ought to seek them of its own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Talent does not petition the world—the world must go out and find it.

sentences.zh: 」薦舉不盡相識，無一失人。

translations.literal: His recommendations did not all involve men he knew personally, yet not one proved a mistaken choice.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended men he did not always know personally, yet never chose wrongly.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓稱其薦賢滿天下，非虛語。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan's remark that his recommendations of worthies filled the empire was no empty phrase.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan said his recommendations of talent had filled the empire, it was no exaggeration.

sentences.zh: 嘗自以聞道晚，刻自繩檢，欿然常若不足。

translations.literal: He considered that he had heard the Way late in life, bound himself with strict self-discipline, and remained humble as though always insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He felt he had come to the Way late, held himself to stern discipline, and stayed modest as if he never measured up.

sentences.zh: 家有田數百畝，初筮仕，誓先墓，不以官俸自益。

translations.literal: His family owned several hundred mu of land; when he first took office he swore before his ancestors' tombs not to enrich himself from official salary.
translations.idiomatic: His family held several hundred mu of land; on first taking office he swore at his ancestors' graves never to pad his private purse with public pay.

sentences.zh: 父著弟子箴言行世，承其志為箴言書院，教人務實學。

translations.literal: His father had written Admonitions for Disciples, which circulated in the world; he carried on that intent in the Zhenyan Academy, teaching people to pursue practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His father had published Admonitions for Disciples; he carried on that aim at the Zhenyan Academy, teaching students practical, useful learning.

sentences.zh: 病革，曰：「吾死，諸君賻吾，惟修書​​院，無贍吾家。

translations.literal: When his illness turned critical he said: "When I die, if you offer funeral gifts, use them only to repair the academy; do not support my household."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said, "If you wish to honor me after I die, give only to the academy—do not provide for my family."

sentences.zh: 」所著讀史兵略、奏議、書牘，皆經世精言。

translations.literal: His works Reading History and Military Stratagems, memorials, and letters were all essential words for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: His Reading History and Military Stratagems, memorials, and correspondence were all classics of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 論曰：駱秉章休休有容，取人為善。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Luo Bingzhang was easy and magnanimous, taking people's good points.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Luo Bingzhang was broad-minded and tolerant, always drawing out the best in others.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼綜覈名實，幹濟冠時。

translations.literal: Hu Linyi synthesized name and reality, and in practical achievement stood foremost in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi matched deeds to names and in practical statesmanship stood above his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 論其治事之寬嚴疏密若不相侔，而皆以長駕遠馭，驅策群材，用能丕樹偉績。

translations.literal: Judging their methods of governing—lax or strict, loose or tight—they seemed incompatible, yet both drove from afar with long reins, spurred on many talents, and thereby could erect great achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Their styles of administration—lenient or stern, loose or tight—seemed worlds apart, yet both governed from a distance, marshaled a host of talent, and thereby built towering achievements.

sentences.zh: 所蒞者千里方圻，規畫動關軍事全局。

translations.literal: The territories they governed spanned a thousand li square, and their plans often touched the overall military situation.
translations.idiomatic: The regions they oversaw sprawled across a thousand li, and their plans routinely shaped the war as a whole.

sentences.zh: 使無其人，則曾國籓、左宗棠諸人失所匡扶憑藉，其成功且較難。

translations.literal: Had these men not existed, Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, and others would have lost the support and leverage that steadied them, and their success would have been far harder.
translations.idiomatic: Without them, Zeng Guofan, Zuo Zongtang, and their peers would have lacked the backing they relied on, and victory would have been far harder to win.

sentences.zh: 緬懷中興之業，二人所關係者豈不鉅哉？

translations.literal: Reflecting on the enterprise of mid-dynasty revival, how vast was what these two men bore upon themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on the revival of the dynasty, how immense was the stake these two men held?
